unruled:gate:household.claims_8862_credi.class: defect: the disallowance question omits the additional child tax credit and credits taken back after an audit

The gated question household.credit_disallowed, as redrafted, names 'a child tax credit, a credit for other dependents or an earned income credit' and its help no longer says that a reduction by letter, audit or court decision, or a credit repaid after an agreed audit, counts: BUG-0862.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 39, '...additional child tax credit, or credit for other dependents for a year after 2015 was denied or reduced'. The question does not name the additional child tax credit; the line source does. A filer whose notice names only the ACTC can answer No and the return claims the credit without Form 8862.

i1040gi p. 43, 'for any reason other than a math or clerical error'. The help gives 'If you are not sure, answer Yes' but no test for what is a math error; a confident filer misclassifies an exam change. Fix in the same entry.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 34, quoted correctly. unruled:gate:sa.gifts#1.class: defect (medium): a filer with 2025 gifts and a carryover can answer sa.charity_limited No; no gate defect in sa.gifts itself
unruled:gate:sa.gifts#1.reason: Finding 0 is covered by sa.gift_carryover. Finding 1: when sa.gifts is Yes, the carryover is asked only inside sa.charity_limited, whose 'is any of them carried over' and '(A limit can apply only when the year's gifts are more than 20% of your income)' invite a No from a filer with small 2025 gifts and an earlier year's carryover. Finding 2: ordinary-income property is covered by gift.deduction's help; the capital-gain-property reductions are a separate low defect. Finding 3 is covered by the K-1 refusals.

findings.evidence: i1040sca p. 11, Line 13. sa.gift_carryover is asked when sa.gifts is No (sa.gift_carryover_if_no_gifts), and a Yes refuses sa.line13.

i1040sca p. 11, Line 13, 'You may have contributions that you couldn't deduct in an earlier year ... you have 5 years to use contributions that were limited in an earlier year.' sa.charity_limited: 'Were your gifts to charity so large that the law limits what you can deduct for 2025, or is any of them carried over from an earlier year? (A limit can apply only when the year's gifts are more than 20% of your income.)' 'Any of them' refers to the 2025 gifts, and the parenthetical denies a limit for small gifts; sa.gift_carryover's plain wording is never asked when sa.gifts is Yes. A No drops line 13 without the refusal.

i1040sca p. 10, item 3, 'You gave gifts of property that increased in value or gave gifts of the use of property' (see Pub. 526); p526, 'The property (other than qualified appreciated stock) is contributed to certain private nonoperating foundations', 'Is put to an unrelated use', 'A contribution of the right to use property ... isn't deductible.' The ordinary-income reduction is in gift.deduction's help; the capital-gain-property reductions and the right to use are not, and gift.deduction asks 'usually what the things would have sold for'. This is a gift.deduction wording defect, not a gate defect.

A partnership's charitable contributions are box 13 codes A to G, refused by k1p.r_b13 ('Box 13 shows an amount with a code other than AE'); an S corporation's are box 12, refused by the k1s box 11/12 question. The form label of sa.gifts also names a K-1 contribution.

unruled:gate:asset.claims_bonus#1.reason: asset.claims_bonus is computed from asset.placed and asset.bonus_choice (≠ none), not a yes/no about "the full or 40% allowance": a 60% claimant would not choose "No: I elect not to take any special allowance". Aircraft, long-production property and QPP are refused (asset.kind_excluded, asset.long_production). The choice wording states the election out. Converted property: asset.placed help counts from the conversion year, and p946 says converted property may be qualified property. Fiscal-year wording is BUG-0565 (5). A spouse transfer is an acquisition from a relative, refused by asset.got_other.

findings.evidence: i4562 p. 6, 60% for "Property with a long production period and certain aircraft". Out of scope: an aircraft is refused by asset.kind_excluded (tick 'A building, land, a vehicle, an aircraft, a film or a recording') and property with a long production period or qualified production property by asset.long_production (tick 'Built to order over a long period, or “qualified production property”'); both feed asset.screen, so asset.screened refuses through asset.cost. Also, asset.claims_bonus is not a yes/no the filer answers: it is asset.bonus_choice ≠ 'none' (choices 'Yes: the special depreciation allowance', 'The 40% allowance...', 'No: I elect not to take any special allowance'), so a filer taking 60% would not pick 'none'.

i4562 p. 7, QPP "by designating up to 100% of the depreciable basis". A used nonresidential building is refused by asset.kind_excluded ("A building, land, ...") and QPP by asset.long_production ("... or “qualified production property”"); either Yes refuses through asset.screened before asset.used_before matters.

i4562 p. 7, "Election out. You can elect, for any class of property, to not deduct any special depreciation allowance". The filer does not answer "is claimed": asset.bonus_choice asks "For property of this kind that you began using in 2025, do you take the special (“bonus”) depreciation allowance?" with the choices "Yes: the special depreciation allowance", the 40% election, and "No: I elect not to take any special allowance". Only an election out gives No, so a filer who made no choice is asked asset.used_before.

i4562 p. 11, Column (b), converted property is placed in service on the conversion date: asset.placed help says "Property you first used personally counts from the year you began using it in the business", so a 2025 conversion is placed in 2025. The premise that the filer's own prior use bars the allowance is contradicted by p946 p. 24: "Property converted from personal use to business use in the same or later tax year may be qualified property."
i4562 p. 9, "assets placed in service during the tax year beginning in 2025". Recorded as BUG-0565 (5): "asset.placed and asset.quarter assume a calendar tax year".

p946 p. 31, original use "whether or not by you". Property a spouse transfers to the other spouse's business is acquired from a relative: asset.got_other ("Did you get it with a trade-in, in an exchange, ..., from a relative or a business you control, or as a gift or inheritance?"; help "a Yes ends the interview here") refuses it through asset.screened.

unruled:gate:asset.industry#1.class: defect (low): BUG-0791, item-defined reuse/recycling property (and, recorded, gathering lines, transmission property and racetracks) owned outside the named businesses skips the industry_item refusal; energy property covered by the class question; others wording
unruled:gate:asset.industry#1.reason: The filer sees the tick "Used in a utility, energy, recycling, rent-to-own, racetrack or loan-financed dealer business" (group "Is it any of these?"), not the encoded "Is your business ...". Energy property is refused through asset.class (Table B-2 F, outside). Reuse and recycling property in a non-recycling business, and gathering lines, transmission lines and race tracks owned outside a utility or track business, miss asset.industry_item and its refusal (BUG-0791). Tense, spouse and floor-plan wording: no defect.

findings.evidence: i4562 p. 10, "Certain energy property specified in section 168(e)(3)(B)(vi)". asset.class offers "Table B-2, D, E and F (alternative energy, biomass and energy property)" (p946 Table B-2 F: "Energy property described in section 48(a)(3)(A) ... solar or wind energy"), mapped to outside, so asset.outside refuses the solar panels, turbine or heat pump whatever the business.

i4562 p. 6, reuse and recycling property is equipment "used exclusively to collect, distribute, or recycle qualified reuse and recyclable materials"; p946, "Unless you elect out, you must take a 50% special depreciation allowance for qualified reuse and recycling property". A manufacturer's baler leaves the tick blank, asset.industry_item_if_industry is false, and the screen does not refuse; with asset.bonus_choice = none the 50% allowance is lost.

p946 p. 31, gathering line 7-year and transmission property 15-year. The tick asks about the business; a non-utility owner leaves it blank and the item list is not asked. Recorded with the reuse/recycling defect.

i4562 p. 9, Line 17. The interview tick is "Used in a ... business", with no tense; a business that has changed since the asset was placed in service is a rare case and the item list (when asked) is about the property. Wording only.

p946 p. 31, "Motorsports entertainment complex. This is a racing track facility permanently situated on land that hosts one or more racing events ... open to the public for the price of admission." A fairground that hosts paid races may leave "racetrack ... business" blank. Recorded with the same bug.

The filer does not see "your business": the interview tick is "Used in a utility, energy, recycling, rent-to-own, racetrack or loan-financed dealer business", asked "For this property" under the Schedule C of the business that uses it, so the spouse's business is the one described.

i4562 p. 7, qualified property excludes "Property described in section 168(k)(9)(A) or 168(k)(9)(B)". The tick says "loan-financed dealer business" and the gated item list states floor plan financing in full ("a loan used to buy motor vehicles, boats, farm machinery or equipment, or trailers or campers held for sale or lease, and secured by them"). Wording only.

unruled:gate:asset.listed#1.class: defect (medium): BUG-0790, listed entertainment property narrowed to camera and recording "equipment"; vehicles refused, pre-2018 peripherals and operator condition recorded (BUG-0565), conversion wording presentation
unruled:gate:asset.listed#1.reason: Vehicles and aircraft are refused by asset.kind_excluded. The redraft prompt drops "phonographic, communication" and says "equipment" where i4562 p. 3 says "Any property used for entertainment or recreational purposes"; a boat or communication equipment used 50% or less is answered No, and the tool depreciates it under GDS instead of refusing (evaluated: $4,000 vs refusal). Pre-2018 peripherals and the operator-owned condition are BUG-0565 (no 2025 depreciation remains).

findings.evidence: i4562 p. 3, transportation property "such as motorcycles, pickup trucks, SUVs, aircraft". A car, SUV, pickup, motorcycle or aircraft is refused by asset.kind_excluded (tick "A building, land, a vehicle, an aircraft, a film or a recording"; help "A car, truck or van is entered with the business's vehicles, not here") through asset.screened; vehicles are scveh entries.

i4562 p. 3: "Any property used for entertainment or recreational purposes (such as photographic, phonographic, communication, and video recording equipment)". The interview prompt reads "equipment of a kind used for entertainment or recreation (such as a camera, or sound or video recording equipment)"; a boat (class 00.28, within the tool) or communication equipment is answered No. Evaluated: $100,000 class 00.28 placed in 2025 at 40% use gives $4,000 on Schedule C line 13 with listed = No; with Yes, asset.listed_low refuses. An RV is a vehicle and is refused by asset.kind_excluded.

i4562 p. 3, exception 2 "Any computer or peripheral equipment ..."; p. 14 "computers and peripheral equipment placed in service before 2018". Recorded as BUG-0565 (1), "asset.listed omits peripherals ... (no 2025 depreciation remains on them)": 5-year property placed before 2018 ended its GDS period by 2022 and its ADS period (5 years for computers and peripherals, p946 ADS table) by 2023.

i4562 p. 3, the employee rule applies to property in exception (1), and exception 2 requires the computer be "owned or leased by the person operating the establishment". The computer condition is BUG-0565 (1) (no 2025 depreciation remains). The employee case is not Schedule C property: asset entries belong to a Schedule C business.

i4562 p. 14, Column (b), converted property placed in service on the conversion date. The pre-2018 computer clause matters only for computers placed before 2018, which have no 2025 depreciation; a computer converted after 2017 answered Yes only adds asset.qbu_low or refuses at 50% or less (a wide error). asset.placed help states the conversion rule. Wording only.

unruled:gate:asset.placed_this_year#1.class: no gate defect; the inverted-gate finding is the review prompt's polarity text (BUG-0800); qualified-use and conversion cases covered
unruled:gate:asset.placed_this_year#1.reason: asset.use_changed is asked exactly when asset.placed_this_year is false (evaluated: a 2023 asset with Yes refuses; a 2025 asset is not asked). A drop in qualified business use that leaves the business share unchanged is caught by asset.qbu_low, asked of listed property every year; the percentage is asked every year and asset.listed_low refuses 50% or less. Converted property: asset.placed help uses the conversion year, and a car is a vehicle refused here.

findings.evidence: i4562 p. 14, listed property recapture. The gate is not inverted. asset.use_changed_if_earlier is Choose [placed_this_year = false → asset.use_changed] [= true → false]: the question is asked exactly for property placed in service before 2025. Evaluated: an asset placed in 2023 with asset.use_changed = Yes gives use_changed_if_earlier true and asset.screened true (refused); with No, $576 of line 17 depreciation; a 2025 asset gives false and is not asked. The review prompt said 'When the condition holds: Choose ... Otherwise: false, and the question below is not asked', the polarity reversal recorded as BUG-0800 (tools/transcription/gates.py).

i4562 p. 14, qualified business use excludes investment use, leasing to a 5% owner or related person, and certain compensation use. asset.qbu_low_if_listed is asked of all listed property, whatever the year placed in service: "Is its business use 50% or less once you leave out these uses, which are not qualified business use?" with those uses listed; Yes refuses through asset.screened, even if asset.use_changed is answered No.

i4562 p. 14, lines 26 and 27 by the 50% test. The tick "The business share of its use has changed" has no "this year": a 2024 drop is still a change since placed in service. The 2025 percentage is asked every year (asset.pct) and asset.listed_low refuses listed property at 50% or less; asset.qbu_low refuses a low qualified business use.

i4562 p. 14, Column (b), "treat the property as placed in service on the date of conversion". asset.placed help: "Property you first used personally counts from the year you began using it in the business." A car is a vehicle, refused by asset.kind_excluded.

unruled:gate:asset.software#1.class: no gate defect; software wording lows (custom code, licences, separately stated software) recorded as presentation; acquired-business software out of scope

unruled:gate:rental.has_commissions#1.reason: (1) spreading a multi-year lease commission rests on text not archived (Pub. 527 lists only 'Commissions'); listed, not ruled a defect. (2) a platform's host fee: wording. (3) covered: group heading.

Insurance paid from a mortgage escrow is paid by the filer through the servicer; the plain tick 'Insurance' under 'Did you pay any of these' covers it, and a help line naming escrow would settle the doubt. Archived Pub. 527 has no escrow sentence for insurance. Low; no bug.

The tick is 'Insurance', not 'landlord insurance', and rental.amt9 asks 'Insurance on it'; any policy on the property counts. unruled:gate:rental.has_loss#1.class: defect: at-risk question reaches only nonrecourse loans from non-lenders (low)
unruled:gate:rental.has_loss#1.reason: Findings 1 to 5 are BUG-0781 (protected amounts, recourse loans from a co-owner or relative, disqualified lenders, property taken subject to debt, the spouse's loan). A prior Form 6198 carryover on a profit year is an open residual on the same entry. Royalties are not rental entries.

findings.evidence: The rental form is rental real estate only (Schedule E types 1 to 5); royalties are $royalty entries ("List each source of royalties"), so rental.not_at_risk is never asked of a royalty property.

i1040se p. 2, At-Risk Rules: not at risk are "Nonrecourse loans used to finance the activity ... not secured by your own property", amounts "protected against loss by a guarantee, stop-loss agreement, or other similar arrangement", and "Amounts borrowed for use in the activity from a person who has an interest in the activity (other than as a creditor) or who is related"; a qualified person "cannot be: Related to you (unless ... commercially reasonable ...), The seller ..., A person who receives a fee due to your investment". rental.not_at_risk asks only "Is any of the money you put into it borrowed on a loan you are not personally liable for, other than a loan from a bank or other lender in the business of lending (for example, a loan from the seller)?" and refuses (Form 6198) at rental.line22 when line 21 is a loss. A loan the filer is personally liable for, from a co-owner or a relative, gives No.

i1040se p. 2, At-Risk Rules: not at risk are "Nonrecourse loans used to finance the activity ... not secured by your own property", amounts "protected against loss by a guarantee, stop-loss agreement, or other similar arrangement", and "Amounts borrowed for use in the activity from a person who has an interest in the activity (other than as a creditor) or who is related"; a qualified person "cannot be: Related to you (unless ... commercially reasonable ...), The seller ..., A person who receives a fee due to your investment". Protected amounts are not borrowed, so the question gives No.

The carve-out exempts every lender in the business of lending, including a related one on non-commercial terms or one with a fee or share in the property.

i6198 p. 1, Amounts Not at Risk 1: "Nonrecourse loans used ... to acquire property used in the activity". Property taken subject to a private nonrecourse mortgage may not read as "money you put into it borrowed".
The question says "you"; on a joint return the spouse's own nonrecourse note on a jointly owned rental is the couple's amount not at risk. Folded into BUG-0781 ("you or your spouse").

i6198 p. 1: a loss limited in an earlier year carries to later years. rental.not_at_risk_if_loss asks only when line 21 is a loss (rental.has_loss), so a Form 6198 carryover in a profit year, or recapture when the at-risk amount falls below zero, is not reached; nothing asks about an earlier Form 6198. findings.evidence: i8839 p. 1, case 1a. s3.adoption_earlier ("Did you ... pay costs in 2024 toward an adoption that was not final at the end of 2024?", help "Yes also for an adoption that was given up or did not succeed") and s3.adoption_us are gated by s3.adoption_any, not by this gate; a Yes refuses s3.line7 with s3.adoption false (fixture redesign.credits.refuse.adoption_earlier_us). i8839 p. 1, case 3b. scope.adoption_benefits ("Did an employer pay or repay any of the adoption costs for you ... Box 12 of a W-2 shows it with the code T"), gated by s3.adoption_any, refuses the return ("A Yes ends the interview here").

i8839 p. 3, "To find out when a foreign adoption is treated as final, see Rev. Proc. 2005-31". A foreign decree in 2024 with a U.S. readoption in 2025 may be answered by the decree date at s3.adoption and at s3.adoption_earlier, so the 2025 credit is lost rather than refused. Medium; remedy a help sentence that a foreign adoption may be final only on a U.S. readoption or recognition.

unruled:gate:s3.adoption_final_if_adopti.class: no gate defect; a not-final adoption gives no 2025 credit that the stepchild question could change; one low residual
unruled:gate:s3.adoption_final_if_adopti.reason: (1-3) model error: s3.adoption_stepchild_if_final is read only by s3.adoption_if_any, which requires a final adoption; a not-final adoption refuses nothing and claims nothing, 2024 payments refuse through s3.adoption_us, and a final non-stepchild adoption refuses. findings.evidence: i8839 p. 2, a spouse's child's expenses are not qualified; p. 3, a U.S. child's 2025 costs on a not-final adoption are credited the year after payment. i8839 p. 3, Domestic Adoption. 2024 payments toward the spouse's child, not final: s3.adoption_earlier and s3.adoption_us (under s3.adoption_any) are Yes and refuse s3.line7 (fixture redesign.credits.refuse.adoption_earlier_us); an over-refusal for a stepchild, safe. The stepchild line is not read on that path.

i8839 p. 3, Rev. Proc. 2005-31 and 2010-31. A filer unsure whether a 2025 foreign decree is final answers No and the credit is lost rather than refused. Low; same remedy as the help sentence on foreign finality.

unruled:gate:person.edu_has_adj#1.reason: The gate (worksheet line 3, the sum of lines 2a to 2c, above zero) is the instructions' line. 'Tax-free help' is defined by the amount question just before. The term question's 'course materials' and 'one term in the year' wording is filed as low.

findings.evidence: person.edu_a_this_year, the question just before, defines the help: 'How much tax-free help with these school costs came in during 2025: scholarships and grants (Form 1098-T box 5), an employer's tuition assistance, veterans' education ...', with help 'only the tax-free part'. A filer who reported employer or VA help there has adjustments above zero and reads 'tax-free help' in the next question as the same items.

i8863 p. 4, lifetime learning credit materials count 'only if required to be paid to the institution'. The interview's person.edu_over asks about 'tuition, required fees and course materials' without that limit (the line's source has it), so an LLC student adds outside books and answers No.
i8863 p. 9, a term beginning January to March 2026 paid in 2025 is treated as beginning in 2025. The help 'With one term in the year, answer by that term alone' can be read as calendar 2025.

person.edu_a_this_year, the question just before, defines the help: 'How much tax-free help with these school costs came in during 2025: scholarships and grants (Form 1098-T box 5), an employer's tuition assistance, veterans' education ...', with help 'only the tax-free part'. It also excludes 'a scholarship reported as income', so the allocation the finding fears is made by the filer's own line 2a entry, which the term question repeats.

person.edu_* is the filer's or spouse's own education (the person collection); a dependent student is asked through dependent.edu with its own questions. The 'For this person (you, or your spouse ...)' frame is right here.

unruled:gate:person.eligible_educator#1.class: no gate defect; the school-year wording is a low residual; the other readings are presentation
unruled:gate:person.eligible_educator#1.reason: As the screen of the same gate: the 900 hours are measured over a school year and the question does not say which; filed. Online schools, several schools and job titles follow the instructions' own list.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 93, 'who worked in a school for at least 900 hours during a school year'. The interview asks 'In 2025, did you work in a school ... for at least 900 hours during a school year?' with no help, so a teacher who left in June 2025 (or started in August 2025) can count only the calendar-2025 hours and answer No; person.educator_expenses_if_educator is then zero (up to $300 lost).
As finding 0, for a teacher who started in August 2025.
i1040gi p. 93, 'worked in a school'. An online K-12 school is a school; the question uses the instructions' words. The suggested help is folded into BUG-0868's fix.
The instructions' test is 900 hours 'in a school' during a school year; the question repeats it. The help in BUG-0868 adds 'count hours at every K-12 school'.

i1040gi p. 93 lists 'teacher, instructor, counselor, principal, or aide'; the question lists the same five. Whether a librarian or coach is an instructor is the instructions' own question; the tool does not narrow it.

unruled:gate:person.has_hsa#1.class: no gate defect; the HSA listing question asks about any HSA held in 2025
unruled:gate:person.has_hsa#1.reason: As the screen of the same gate: the $f8889 question includes an HSA with no 2025 activity, so a dormant HSA with an old excess is asked and refused. Citation filed.

findings.evidence: $f8889: 'Did you have a health savings account (HSA) in 2025, or get money from one?', help 'Answer Yes even if nothing went in or out in 2025'. A person with an HSA still holding an old excess (the account exists in 2025) lists it, and person.x_hsa_prior_excess is asked and refuses through person.x_other.

The help names the signs of an HSA (W-2 box 12 code W, Form 5498-SA or 1099-SA) and says to answer Yes with no 2025 activity; an account held at a brokerage is still 'a health savings account'. A filer who does not know they have an HSA cannot be reached by any wording.
Citation of person.has_hsa and person.x_hsa_prior_excess(_if_hsa): Parts II and IX instead of Part VII.

unruled:gate:person.ira_files_8606#1.class: no gate defect; earlier basis with a 2025 distribution is refused on the Form 1099-R; basis from a rollover, divorce or decedent is a low residual
unruled:gate:person.ira_files_8606#1.reason: Findings 0 and 1 are refused through retirement.ira_basis on the traditional IRA Form 1099-R; reservist repayments and recharacterizations are refused by their own questions; for-2025 contributions made in 2026 are counted; line 1 is figured, not labelled by the filer. Basis that is not the filer's own undeducted contribution is filed.

findings.evidence: Each traditional IRA Form 1099-R (distribution or conversion) asks retirement.ira_basis, 'Have you ever put money into a traditional IRA that you did not deduct on a tax return?' (help: 'If any of your earlier tax returns includes Form 8606, answer Yes. ... a Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses through retirement.special. The gate person.ira_files_8606 opens line 2 only for a 2025 nondeductible contribution; basis from earlier years with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the 1099-R.

Each traditional IRA Form 1099-R (distribution or conversion) asks retirement.ira_basis, 'Have you ever put money into a traditional IRA that you did not deduct on a tax return?' (help: 'If any of your earlier tax returns includes Form 8606, answer Yes. ... a Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses through retirement.special. The gate person.ira_files_8606 opens line 2 only for a 2025 nondeductible contribution; basis from earlier years with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the 1099-R. The 2025 conversion of the 2024 contribution comes on a 1099-R from the traditional IRA; the filer reported Form 8606 for 2024, so the help 'If any of your earlier tax returns includes Form 8606, answer Yes' gives Yes.

i8606 p. 9, Line 2, after-tax plan money rolled to a traditional IRA. retirement.ira_basis asks whether the filer 'put money into a traditional IRA that you did not deduct'; a rollover may not read as that, and no Form 8606 may exist. The whole distribution is then taxed (overstated).

i8606 p. 2, a divorce transfer that changes basis. The receiving spouse made no undeducted contribution and answers No to retirement.ira_basis; person.ira_basis_adjusted, which names divorce transfers, is asked only of a person filing Form 8606 for 2025.
i8606 p. 2, 'a distribution from an inherited traditional IRA that has a basis'. The beneficiary answers retirement.ira_basis for their own contributions and says No.
i8606 p. 9, Line 1 includes a qualified reservist repayment; scope.reservist_repaid (ira.reservist_repaid) refuses the IRA deduction special case, so the return is refused whatever line 1 shows.
person.ira_recharacterized, 'Did you recharacterize a 2025 contribution (move it from a traditional to a Roth IRA or the reverse)?', refuses through the IRA excess/recharacterized screen.
person.sav_trad (which gates person.ira_trad): 'Money put in by April 15, 2026 for 2025 counts'; the nondeductible part follows from those contributions.

person.ira_nondeductible is person.ira_nd_figured, 'the smaller of line 10 or 11, less line 12' of the IRA Deduction Worksheet (i8606 p. 9, Line 1); the filer enters total traditional contributions and is never asked to label them nondeductible.

unruled:gate:person.ira_owner#1.class: no gate defect; minor UNCLEARs answered by 'If you are not sure, answer Yes'
unruled:gate:person.ira_owner#1.reason: The help says 'If you are not sure, answer Yes', and the misses understate Roth contributions or saver's credit (the filer's loss) or need an uncorrected failed rollover.

findings.evidence: Help: 'A 401(k) or a pension at work is not an IRA. If you are not sure, answer Yes.' A state auto-IRA is a Roth IRA in the employee's name; a filer unsure of its kind is told to answer Yes. A No loses only Roth contributions from the saver's credit (person.sav_roth), the filer's loss.

The line's source says 'individual retirement arrangement'; the interview says 'individual retirement account'. An IRA annuity owner is told IRAs of any kind count and, if unsure, to answer Yes. Rare.
A rollover IRA is an IRA in name and on its statements; the help's 'A 401(k) ... is not an IRA' refers to the plan at work. A failed second rollover left as an excess is rare.

unruled:gate:person.mw_has_1099#1.class: no gate defect; without a Form 1099 the payments are treated the same way the Schedule C route would
unruled:gate:person.mw_has_1099#1.reason: The business question only moves nontaxable payments between line 1d/8s and Schedule C; the amounts net to the same tax. The other findings are about recognizing the payments as Medicaid waiver payments, which the scope question's help names.

findings.evidence: Without a Form 1099 the payments not in W-2 box 1 are person.mw_other: they go on line 1d only if the person chooses them as earned income (person.mw_other_1d) and are then excluded on Schedule 1 line 8s (person.line8s), or else stay out of income. i1040sc p. 6 nets excludable Medicaid waiver payments to zero on Schedule C ('report the nontaxable and excludable amount as an expense in Part V'). The tax and the earned-income choice are the same; only the form the amounts would appear on differs (amb.2025.mw_all_nontaxable).

scope.medicaid_waiver asks 'did a state Medicaid program pay you ... to care for someone who lives in your home?', help 'These are Medicaid waiver payments, also called difficulty of care payments'. A caregiver who does not recognize the pay reports it as ordinary income, which overstates tax (the filer's loss).
As finding 0: a home-care sole proprietor who answers No because no Schedule C has been prepared gets line 1d and Schedule 1 line 8s amounts with the same tax.

unruled:gate:person.mw_has_not_box1#1.class: no gate defect; the not-in-box-1 question names Forms 1099 and no form
unruled:gate:person.mw_has_not_box1#1.reason: person.mw_not_box1 asks 'How much of that Medicaid pay is not in box 1 of a W-2: shown only in box 12 with code II, on a Form 1099-MISC or 1099-NEC, or on no form?', so a filer with only a 1099 is asked the 1099 amount.

findings.evidence: person.mw_not_box1's question names 'on a Form 1099-MISC or 1099-NEC, or on no form'; a filer with no W-2 enters the 1099 amount, person.mw_has_not_box1 is true and person.mw_1099 is asked.
The amount questions ask amounts, not the election; the election is person.mw_earned, asked after. The 1099 amount goes on line 1d regardless (person.line1d sums person.mw_1099_if_not_box1).

As gate:person.mw_has_1099 finding 1: the scope question's help names 'Medicaid waiver payments, also called difficulty of care payments'; a filer who does not recognize the pay reports it as income, overstating tax.

unruled:gate:person.mw_paid#1.class: no gate defect; the total includes 1099 and no-form payments, and the earned-income choice follows i1040gi Step 5
unruled:gate:person.mw_paid#1.reason: person.mw_total = person.mw_box1_if_mw + person.mw_not_box1_if_mw, and the second names Forms 1099 and no form. The earned-income choice applies to all nontaxable payments excluded on line 8s (i1040gi p. 42, Step 5).

findings.evidence: person.mw_total sums W-2 box 1 and person.mw_not_box1, whose question includes 'on a Form 1099-MISC or 1099-NEC, or on no form'. A parent paid through a fiscal intermediary with no W-2 has a total above zero and is asked person.mw_earned.

person.mw_box1's help: 'Box 12 code II shows such pay that is not in box 1'; the scope help names difficulty of care payments. A filer who omits a $0-box-1 W-2 loses only the earned-income choice (nontaxable either way).
The questions say 'someone who lives in your home'; pay for care while the person lived there is the pay asked about. A filer who omits it reports it as income, the filer's loss. Rare.

i1040gi p. 42, Step 5: 'Enter the Medicaid waiver payment amounts excluded from income on Schedule 1, line 8s, unless you choose to include these amounts in earned income'. Box 1 amounts are on line 1a and excluded on line 8s (person.line8s includes person.mw_box1_if_mw); the choice then applies to them as the instructions say (person.mw_not_earned). The line 1a entry is not dropped.

unruled:gate:person.rmd_possible#1.class: no gate defect in the birth-year/inherited gate for yearly RMDs; the question's 'yearly minimum' wording misses deadline-type requirements (filed)
unruled:gate:person.rmd_possible#1.reason: The gate admits everyone born in 1952 or earlier and every beneficiary, which covers yearly RMDs, inherited Roth accounts and spousal beneficiaries. The question's 'required yearly minimum' misses the 5-year/10-year deadline and the April 1 first-year distribution, and the gate misses a QDRO alternate payee; filed as one medium entry.

findings.evidence: i5329 p. 9, 'You owe this tax if you don't receive the minimum required distribution from your qualified retirement plan'. An alternate payee's QDRO share is neither 'inherited' nor timed by the payee's birth year; person.rmd_possible is false. Rare.

i5329 p. 9, 'The tax is due for the tax year that includes the last day by which the minimum required distribution must be taken'. A beneficiary who had to empty the account by December 31, 2025 had no 'yearly minimum' and answers No; 25% of the remaining balance is missed.

The help says 'people who inherited an account, usually must take a minimum amount out each year', which tells a 10-year beneficiary that a yearly amount usually applies. Folded into BUG-0870's rewording.

The gate's inherited question covers any inherited IRA or workplace account, Roth included, and the help says inherited accounts usually need yearly withdrawals; the miss needs a filer who overrides the help.

person.inherited_account: 'Have you inherited an IRA or a workplace retirement account ... from someone who died?' A spouse beneficiary inherited from someone who died; a surviving spouse born in 1952 or earlier is in the gate anyway.
The first distribution of a person born in 1951 (for 2024) was due April 1, 2025; 'the required yearly minimum ... by its deadline' can be read as 2025's amount only.
'A retirement account' is plain language for IRAs and plans, including 457(b) and 403(b); the line's source says 'an IRA or plan'. Low.
'A Yes ends the interview here' is the tool's standard notice for every refusing question (protocol norm); it states the consequence truthfully.

unruled:gate:person.sav_trad_if_ira_owne.class: no gate defect; the questions count 2026 contributions for 2025; a contribution not yet made is not recorded
unruled:gate:person.sav_trad_if_ira_owne.reason: person.ira_owner counts an IRA 'opened in early 2026 for 2025' and person.sav_trad 'Money put in by April 15, 2026 for 2025'. Backdoor and SEP readings are presentation; recharacterization is refused by its own question.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 98, line 11, 'made, or that will be made by the due date'. A filer who has not yet opened or funded the IRA cannot report it; opening and funding it before filing answers both questions Yes (help 'one opened in early 2026 for 2025'). Not a gate defect.
person.sav_trad: 'Did you put money into a traditional IRA for 2025? Money put in by April 15, 2026 for 2025 counts'.
The question is framed 'For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return)' and asks whether money was put into a traditional IRA for that person; who funded it does not change the answer.
Help: 'It counts whether or not you can deduct it.' A backdoor contribution is a traditional IRA contribution the filer made; the later conversion is on a 1099-R where retirement.ira_basis refuses.
person.ira_recharacterized asks 'Did you recharacterize a 2025 contribution (move it from a traditional to a Roth IRA or the reverse)?' and refuses.
The help excludes SEP plan contributions; a personal (non-SEP) contribution to a SEP-IRA is rare and a No understates the deduction (the filer's loss).

unruled:gate:person.simple_open_year#1.class: no gate defect; 1963 to 1965 is the 60 to 63 band by birth year; the January 1, 1966 wording is the low residual
unruled:gate:person.simple_open_year#1.reason: As the screen of the same gate; the gate is per person; only the January 1 wording residual remains.

findings.evidence: person.simple_age sends birth years 1963 to 1965 to person.simple_age_60_63_years, which returns person.catchup_age60_63 when person.simple_open_year is false; the gate's otherwise value is read only for 1962 and 1966.
person.birth_year is each person's own entry (person collection), so the spouse's gate tests the spouse's birth year.

p560 p. 16, 'attain age 60'; the January 1, 1966 participant attains 60 on December 31, 2025 under the day-before rule, but person.simple_age_at_year_end asks 'How old were you at the end of 2025?' with no rule.

unruled:gate:person.turned_65_this_year#.class: no gate defect; the MFS spouse's boxes are refused elsewhere; the 'final return' wording is a low residual
unruled:gate:person.turned_65_this_year#.reason: On a separate return the spouse's age box is not figured from a spouse record: sa.spouse_extra refuses it. The joint-return widow reading is filed as low.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d, MFS spouse boxes. The tool does not figure them: sa.spouse_extra ('Did your husband or wife have no income in 2025, and are they filing no 2025 return, and were they born before January 2, 1961, or blind ...?', a Yes refuses) handles a separate return. Over-refusal for a spouse who died before 65, never a wrong box.

For the spouse's record on a joint return the question reads 'Is this the final return of a person who died in 2025 before reaching age 65?'; a surviving spouse may answer No, giving the age box and senior deduction wrongly. Rare.

The interview is answered for the taxpayer named on the return ('you'); an executor answering for a decedent answers for that person throughout. The help 'For a living person the answer is No' refers to the person the record is for.

unruled:gate:person.under16_open_year#1.class: no gate defect; a filer born 2011 or later is under 16 by birth year and refused
unruled:gate:person.under16_open_year#1.reason: As the screen of the same gate.

findings.evidence: person.under16 = 'birth_year > 2010' or (born 2010 and the answer). A filer born in 2011 or later is under 16 and refused by household.filer_under16 (amb.2025.filer_under_16) without the question.

unruled:gate:person.x_edu_account#1.class: no gate defect for dormant accounts or owners; four rare residuals filed together; citation filed
unruled:gate:person.x_edu_account#1.reason: The gate asks about holding an account in 2025, so a dormant Coverdell with an old excess and an owner's own withdrawal are asked. A Coverdell opened in 2026 for 2025, a deemed distribution and credit-coordinated costs are low residuals; the citation is filed.

findings.evidence: The interview asks 'At any time in 2025, did you have a 529 plan, a Coverdell education savings account or an ABLE account, or was one held for you?' (help 'Answer Yes whether the account is yours or is held for you'). f5329 Part V, contributions 'for 2025' can be made through April 15, 2026; an account opened then did not exist in 2025, so the beneficiary answers No and the 6% tax on the excess is missed. Rare.

The interview asks 'At any time in 2025, did you have a 529 plan, a Coverdell education savings account or an ABLE account, or was one held for you?' (help 'Answer Yes whether the account is yours or is held for you'). The account existed in 2025, so the beneficiary answers Yes and person.x_edu_excess (help 'This includes an excess from an earlier year') refuses. The 'contributions or distributions' wording is the line's label, not the question (BUG-0865).

p970: a Coverdell balance is treated as distributed at 30 or death. person.x_edu_taxable asks whether money that 'came out of the account in 2025' was taxable; a deemed distribution with no payment reads as No.

x_edu_taxable's help 'Money used for the costs the account is meant for is not taxable' does not say that costs used for an education credit or paid by tax-free help do not count, so a partly taxable 529 distribution reads as No.

The interview asks 'At any time in 2025, did you have a 529 plan, a Coverdell education savings account or an ABLE account, or was one held for you?' (help 'Answer Yes whether the account is yours or is held for you'). An owner of a 529 or Coverdell has an account that 'is yours' and answers Yes.
The gate's and gated lines' locator quotes Part IX (RMD) and omits Parts V and VIII.

unruled:gate:dependent.edu_has_adj#1.class: no gate defect; the gate is total adjustments (worksheet line 3) above zero, as labeled
unruled:gate:dependent.edu_has_adj#1.reason: dependent.edu_has_adj is 'dependent.edu_adj > 0', and dependent.edu_adj is 'Adjusted Qualified Education Expenses Worksheet, line 3 ... add lines 2a, 2b and 2c' (edu_adj_sum), so any tax-free help or refund asks dependent.edu_over, whose Yes refuses. The kinds of help are listed in the preceding question; the per-term reading is in the question. One low wording residual on books for the lifetime learning credit.

findings.evidence: Verified: dependent.edu_adj is worksheet line 3 (edu_adj_sum of lines 2a to 2c), not line 4; a period whose help exceeds its expenses has line 3 above zero and the question is asked.

i8863 p. 4. The amount question just before (dependent.edu_a_this_year) defines the help for the filer: 'scholarships and grants (Form 1098-T box 5), an employer's tuition assistance, veterans' education benefits'; dependent.edu_refunds asks the refunds.

i8863 p. 9, period beginning in the first 3 months of 2026. The question is 'Was there a school term for which the tax-free help and the refunds came to more than what was paid in 2025 for that term's tuition...' and the help says 'Count help and refunds received in 2025 or in 2026 before you file'; it does not limit the term to one held in 2025.
i8863 p. 9, separate worksheet per period. The question asks whether there was 'a school term for which' help exceeded that term's costs; netting the year is not the question asked.

i8863 p. 4, books for the lifetime learning credit only if paid to the institution. 'course materials' is unqualified in the question; the amount question dependent.edu_inst asks only institution-required materials. A misreading matters only with two or more terms (with one term the computed line 4 is already zero). Low.

unruled:gate:dependent.ever_married#1.class: one low wording residual: the help does not name common-law marriage
unruled:gate:dependent.ever_married#1.reason: dependent.ever_married gates dependent.joint_return and dependent.married (whose Yes refuses a married dependent). Its help says only 'Count a marriage that has since ended'; the line source names death, divorce or annulment but not common-law or foreign/tribal marriage, while household.ever_married's help names common-law marriage. BUG-0863 (shared with the household marriage questions).

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 21, Married person; p501 p. 6, common-law marriage. A common-law married dependent who files jointly can be answered No and the joint-return refusal is skipped; the help does not say a common-law marriage counts.

A filer who believes the person never married would answer an ungated joint-return question ('Is a joint tax return for 2025 being filed that includes this person...') No as well: the filer's knowledge, not the gate, decides. No defect in the gate.
An annulment after 2025 is covered by 'Count a marriage that has since ended'. A religious or tribal ceremony that is a marriage under state law is not named; as finding 0.

unruled:gate:dependent.other_only_spouse.class: no gate defect; every No leads to the tie-breaker refusal
unruled:gate:dependent.other_only_spouse.reason: On a separate return a No to dependent.other_only_spouse sets spouse_settles false; dependent.tiebreak_other then refuses at dependent.qc_tiebreak whenever dependent.other_claimant is Yes and the other is a taxpayer or the child is also the filer's qualifying child. The spouse's claim is refused, not ignored. The spouse-claims question is asked only in the Example 6 case the tool computes.

findings.evidence: p501 p. 15. Executed (fixture mfsl4.other_relative_too, married filing separately, other_claimant Yes, other_only_spouse No): other_only_spouse_if_mfs false, spouse_settles false, tiebreak_other true, and f1040.line19, dependent[kid].ctc_amount and line 27a refuse at dependent[kid].qc_tiebreak / eic_tiebreak ('The tie-breaker rules are outside this tool').

p501 p. 17, release to the noncustodial parent. A married couple living apart answers dependent.parents_apart Yes (separated, or lived apart the last 6 months); dependent.divorced_rule ('given the right to claim the child to the other parent, by signing Form 8332 or under a divorce decree...') Yes refuses (dependent.divorced_rule_screen). A couple who lived together in the last 6 months is outside the rule (i1040gi p. 20).

p501 p. 17, Example 6. The question asks a fact ('the only relative, besides you, who lived with this child for more than half of 2025'); an unsure No refuses at dependent.qc_tiebreak (executed, finding 0). Errs toward refusal.
A stepparent spouse: a No refuses at dependent.qc_tiebreak (tiebreak_other true, the child being the filer's qualifying child), as finding 0. Errs toward refusal.

unruled:gate:dependent.ptc_files#1.class: defect: the question states only the single under-65 non-blind limits and does not name a taxable scholarship as pay
unruled:gate:dependent.ptc_files#1.reason: dependent.ptc_files sets whether the dependent's modified AGI enters f8962 line 2b. Married dependents and Form 8814 are refused elsewhere; the combined test is in the help. A taxable scholarship is not named as pay, and whether the self-employment rule is an income filing threshold is not settled or asked: BUG-0861.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 10, Chart B married dependents. A dependent who has ever been married is asked dependent.married, whose Yes refuses ('A married dependent is outside this tool', dependent.married_screen_qc).

i1040gi p. 10, combined test. The help shown with the question: 'A dependent with both kinds must also file when the two together are more than the larger of $1,350 and their pay (up to $15,300) plus $450.'

i1040gi p. 10, Chart B: 'Earned income includes salaries, wages, tips, professional fees, and taxable scholarship and fellowship grants.' The question says 'pay' and never names a taxable scholarship; a dependent with $16,500 of taxable scholarship answers No and the modified AGI is left out of line 2b (PTC overstated).
i8962 p. 8, Form 8814. Form 8814 is refused: scope.f8814 Yes refuses f1040.line16 (scope.other_line16).

i8962 p. 8, 'required to file ... because their income meets the income tax return filing threshold'. Whether $400 of net self-employment earnings is such a threshold is not settled by the cited text; the question does not ask it. Recorded in the same entry for a source decision.

unruled:gate:dependent.relationship#1.class: no gate defect; the gated parent question is read only on a separate return
unruled:gate:dependent.relationship#1.reason: dependent.filer_parent (gated by relationship = child) is read only through dependent.spouse_settles_unclaimed, which is reached only when dependent.other_only_spouse_if_mfs is true (married filing separately). On a joint return it is never consulted. Its No refuses at the tie-breaker; the relationship answer list names adopted and placed children.

findings.evidence: Verified: the only consumer of dependent.filer_parent_if_child is dependent.spouse_settles_unclaimed (forms/2025/dependent.yaml), under spouse_settles, which is false unless household.mfs. On a joint return the stepparent's No changes nothing.
i1040gi p. 20, adopted child. The relationship answer the filer picks from reads 'My son or daughter (adopted or placed for adoption included), my stepchild, a foster child...'.

i1040gi p. 20, a child lawfully placed for adoption is an adopted child. The parent question ('Are you this child's parent by birth or by adoption?') does not say a pending placement counts; on a separate return a No refuses at dependent.qc_tiebreak, never a wrong amount. Low.

p501 p. 19, local law (a member-of-household rule). The relationship help 'Choose the last answer if your relationship with the person broke local law' is general; a parent who picks 'Someone else' for their own child is implausible given the first answer 'My son or daughter'. Low.

unruled:gate:household.all_tin#1.class: no gate defect; the TIN questions state the due-date and renewal rules
unruled:gate:household.all_tin#1.reason: household.all_tin is computed (household.tin_count = household.persons) from person.tin and person.itin_applied, whose wording follows i8863 p. 3 requirement 5. The filer never sees the gate's citation.

findings.evidence: i8863 p. 3, TIN issued by the due date including extensions. person.tin's help: 'The number must be issued by the date the 2025 return is due, extensions included.' A filer answering before the SSN is issued answers No; the return cannot carry the number until it is issued. Low.
person.tin asks 'Do you have a social security number, or an ITIN ...?' with no employment-validity condition; the CTC text the reviewer cites is not shown with it. A restricted SSN reads as Yes.

person.tin help: 'An ITIN that has expired counts only once it has been renewed; an application to renew is not enough.' person.itin_applied: 'Have you applied, or are you applying, for an ITIN or for the renewal of your expired ITIN, by the date the 2025 return is due?' (help: 'Answer Yes if you are applying with this return').

The gate is computed and not shown; the filer answers person.tin and person.itin_applied, which do not mention dependents. The AOC lines (person.edu_aoc_tin, dependent.edu_aoc_tin) cite i8863 p. 3 requirement 5.

unruled:gate:household.marriage_possible.class: no gate defect; the gate's question names common-law marriage and the domestic partner question is asked apart from it
unruled:gate:household.marriage_possible.reason: household.marriage_possible is household.ever_married for single and head of household. Its help: 'Count a marriage that has ended, and a common-law marriage. A registered domestic partnership or civil union is not a marriage.' Registered domestic partners are asked household.rdp independently of any marriage, and household.rdp_community_property refuses at f1040 (forms/2025/f1040.yaml).

findings.evidence: The gate question's own help names common-law marriage: household.ever_married, 'Count a marriage that has ended, and a common-law marriage.'

i1040gi p. 23, Nevada, Washington and California domestic partners. household.rdp ('At any time in 2025, were you a registered domestic partner in Nevada, Washington or California?' help: 'A Yes ends the interview here') is not gated by marriage; household.rdp_community_property (status not mfj, community property, rdp) refuses on f1040 line 118's refusal list.

p501 p. 6, Annulled marriages. The help 'Count a marriage that has ended' reads naturally to include an annulled one; the quasi-community property point is state-law detail beyond the cited text. Low.

unruled:gate:household.married#1.class: no gate defect; the widow case is refused by its own screen; low wording residual on common-law, foreign marriage and informal separation
unruled:gate:household.married#1.reason: household.married = marriage_possible then married_dec31. A filer whose spouse died in 2025 and who chose single or head of household is asked household.spouse_died_this_year ('If you chose a line for an unmarried person, a Yes ends the interview here'), and household.widowed_this_year refuses on f1040.line12e. Interlocutory decree and divorce-and-remarriage are in married_dec31's help. Common-law marriage, foreign or tribal marriage and informal separation are in the line source (BUG-0280) but not in the help shown: BUG-0863.

findings.evidence: p501 p. 6, Spouse died during the year. household.spouse_died_this_year is asked of a single or head of household filer who has been married (household.spouse_died_this_year_if_ever_married), and household.widowed_this_year refuses ('Filing status after a spouse's death in 2025', on f1040.line12e). married_dec31's help says to answer No for a spouse who died, by design.
p501 p. 6, common-law marriage. The gate's help (household.ever_married) names it; married_dec31's help does not.

p501 p. 6, 'married and living apart but not legally separated under a decree'. married_dec31's help lists only decrees ending a marriage; it does not say that living apart or a separation agreement does not. The line source does.
married_dec31 help: 'A divorce that was not yet final on December 31 means you were still married'.
married_dec31 help: '... unless you divorced only to file as unmarried and married each other again in 2026.'
p501 p. 6, Definition of marriage. Foreign or tribal marriages recognized by a state are in the line source, not the help.

unruled:gate:household.mfs#1.class: no gate defect; one low wording residual in the spouse-only help
unruled:gate:household.mfs#1.reason: household.mfs (f1040.status = mfs) gates household.mfs_living and dependent.other_only_spouse. Off MFS, mfs_living's consumers are MFS-only rules and the head of household lived-apart test is household.considered_unmarried; on head of household the spouse's competing claim reaches the tie-breaker refusal. A filer with no other claimant is not refused. The help 'another parent of the child' contradicts the question on a separate return: BUG-0864.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 15. Head of household for a married filer reads household.considered_unmarried ('You lived apart from your husband or wife for the last six months of 2025, ...'), asked of anyone married on December 31; household.mfs_living_if_mfs feeds only MFS rules (ssb, eic.mfs_same_home, f2441 line A, ira, s1, person).

i1040gi p. 17. On head of household the gate is false, spouse_settles false, and dependent.other_claimant (help 'On a separate return, your husband or wife counts') Yes refuses at dependent.qc_tiebreak. Executed (fixture mfsl4.other_relative_too, married filing separately, other_claimant Yes, other_only_spouse No): other_only_spouse_if_mfs false, spouse_settles false, tiebreak_other true, and f1040.line19, dependent[kid].ctc_amount and line 27a refuse at dependent[kid].qc_tiebreak / eic_tiebreak ('The tie-breaker rules are outside this tool').

p501 p. 17, Example 6. The help 'Answer No if a grandparent, aunt, uncle, grown brother or sister, or another parent of the child also lived with the child' names the spouse, who is the child's other parent; a No refuses at dependent.qc_tiebreak in the case the tool computes. Refusal only; low.

i1040gi p. 17. Executed (mfsl4.other_relative_too with other_claimant No): qc_tiebreak false, no refusal, f1040.line19 $2,200 (ctc_amount $2,200), eic_child true. The No to other_only_spouse does not refuse when no one else could claim the child (the help says 'may').

i1040gi p. 32, worksheet line 8. The answer 'Not at any time in 2025' is not true of a filer who lived with the spouse at times; the help counts time away for work as living together, which makes together the answer.

unruled:gate:f1040.digital_assets#1.class: defect: airdrops not named in the gated question and passive rewards read as holding (BUG-0896)
unruled:gate:f1040.digital_assets#1.reason: Line 8v's IRS list is open ('for example ... forks, staking, or mining'); the gated question is closed and the gate help frames passive credits as holding.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8v, 'for example, digital assets, such as income from forks, staking, or mining'. s1.digital_income asks only 'from staking, from mining that is not a business, or when a coin split in two (a fork)', so an airdrop is answered No. Promotional or learn-and-earn rewards are prizes or awards asked by s1.winnings_any ('receive a prize or an award'), not line 8v.

As screen finding 0: the help 'Buying crypto with dollars and holding it ... is a No' with Yes examples limited to being paid, swapping and spending invites a No from a holder whose exchange credited staking rewards.

The question says 'crypto or another digital asset'; a stablecoin is a digital asset by the plain words, and the help does not exclude it. Low; noted in BUG-0896's discussion of naming examples, not a separate defect.
Forked coins credited without action: same help wording as finding 1 (i1040gi p. 16, 'Received digital assets as a result of a hard fork').

unruled:gate:f1040.estimated_any#1.class: defect: gate wording misses amended-return credits and joint payments by a spouse or former spouse (BUG-0897); separate-return share BUG-0894
unruled:gate:f1040.estimated_any#1.reason: As the screen review; separate returns are now supported, so the separate filer case is live.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 39, joint estimated tax on separate returns. On a separate return 'you (or, on a joint return, your spouse)' reads as the filer only, and the help says 'ones you send yourself', so joint payments sent by the spouse are answered No.
i1040gi p. 39, divorced taxpayers with joint payments; a former spouse is not mentioned.
i1040gi p. 39, 'from your 2024 return or an amended return'; the gate names only a 2024 refund.
'have a 2024 refund applied' versus Form 1040 line 26 'amount applied from 2024 return'; low part of the same entry.
The prompt says 'for 2025' but the help says 'during the year'; a January 2026 fourth-quarter payment may be left out. Low part of the same entry.
'send the IRS estimated tax payments' covers any method of payment in plain reading; the help describes timing, not the method. Low; BUG-0897's help change also names online and card payments.
The amount question f1040.line26 gives only joint-return help; a separate filer can enter the whole joint payment (completeness f1040#1.6).

unruled:gate:f1040.withheld_other_any#1.class: defect (low): Forms 8805 and 8288-A not named (BUG-0898); the other findings are covered by the help
unruled:gate:f1040.withheld_other_any#1.reason: The help points to 'box 4 of a Form 1099 or W-2G' and says 'If you are not sure, answer Yes'.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 39, Line 25c, Form 8805. As screen finding 0.
i1040gi p. 39, Line 25c, Form 8288-A. As screen finding 1. A nonresident seller is refused by scope.nonresident; a resident seller who gave no certification is the remaining case.
i1040gi p. 39, Line 25b, 1099-R box 4. The help says 'Look for box 4 of a Form 1099' and the prompt names a pension; a conversion is reported on Form 1099-R with box 4.
Backup withholding on Form 1099-NEC, 1099-MISC or 1099-K is box 4 of a Form 1099, which the help names; 'other than wages' does not exclude it on the help's own test.
Backup withholding on 1099-B, -INT or -DIV is box 4 of a Form 1099, named by the help.
A fiscal-year partnership's K-1 withholding: the help says 'Tax withheld on a Schedule K-1 ... counts too' without a timing limit; low.
Form 1042-S is named in the help ('Tax withheld on a Schedule K-1 or Form 1042-S counts too').
