f1040.digital_assets (interview): 'In 2025, did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) receive, sell, trade, spend or give away crypto'; the spouse is named on page 1 and in s1.digital_income.

i1040gi p. 92, Line 8v. The closed list in s1.digital_income ('staking, ... mining that is not a business, or ... a fork') is the second half of BUG-0896, whose fix adds airdrops and 'a similar activity'.

i1040gi p. 92, Line 8v. The interview asks the fact ('Did you ... receive any crypto from staking, from mining that is not a business, or when a coin split in two (a fork)?'), not 'as ordinary income'; a filer who believes staking is untaxed until sale still answers Yes to receiving it. Business mining belongs on Schedule C, as the help says.
i1040gi p. 92, 'If, in 2025, you received'. The timing of locked staking rewards (dominion and control) is a legal question the instructions do not settle; low.

i1040gi p. 92, Line 8v. A dollar bonus from a crypto platform is ordinary income not received as a digital asset; it is other income, entered in the oi8z collection (line 8z). Placement only; total income is the same.

unruled:gate:s1.has_gambling#1.class: no gate defect; finding 4 rides with the winnings-gate defect
unruled:gate:s1.has_gambling#1.reason: Finding 0 is a model error: the gate is computed from s1.gambling_winnings, whose asked wording has no business exclusion. Finding 1 model error (spouse named). Findings 2 and 3 covered by the amount question's wording and help. Finding 4 is the s1.winnings_any timing defect.

findings.evidence: The gambling winnings question s1.gambling_winnings asks 'How much did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) win from gambling in 2025, before subtracting any losses?' with help naming W-2G box 1, lotteries, raffles, sports bets and fantasy sports; it has no trade-or-business exclusion, so a professional's winnings are entered and s1.has_gambling holds.
s1.winnings_any and s1.gambling_winnings both say '(or, on a joint return, your spouse)'; the spouse's winnings make s1.has_gambling true.
p525 p. 33. s1.gambling_winnings asks winnings 'before subtracting any losses' and help 'Losses are asked with deductions'; a losing year still has gross winnings.
p525 p. 33, 'Winnings from fantasy sports leagues are gambling winnings.' s1.gambling_winnings help names 'sports bets, fantasy sports'; poker is gambling in ordinary usage.
p525 p. 33, Installment payments; i1040gi p. 91, Line 8b. The winnings gate asks what was won in 2025; the fix keys it to receipt.

unruled:gate:s1.nol_joint#1.class: no gate defect; finding 0 is caught by the non-joint branch, and finding 1 rides with the NOL wording low
unruled:gate:s1.nol_joint#1.reason: Finding 0 is a model error: a QSS, single or HOH filer has s1.nol_separate true and is asked s1.nol_was_joint ('Did you file a joint return for the year any of the loss arose, or for any year from then to 2024?'), whose Yes refuses. Finding 1 (an excess business loss not known as an NOL) is a scope.nol help low. Finding 2 presentation; finding 3 out of scope (scope.k1); finding 4 presentation.

findings.evidence: i172 p. 3, Change in Marital Status and Joint to separate returns. s1.nol_separate (scope.nol and status not mfj) gates s1.nol_was_joint; a widow or divorced filer whose loss came from a joint year answers Yes and s1.line8a refuses on s1.nol_marital.

i172 p. 4, Excess Business Loss, 'Excess business losses that are disallowed are treated as an NOL carryover to the following tax year'. scope.nol (tick 'A loss still being carried into 2025 (a 'net operating loss')', help 'A loss bigger than that year's income') does not name a loss held back by the Form 461 limit; a No loses a deduction (no wrong refusal). Low.
i172 p. 3. scope.nol already asks '(or, on a joint return, your spouse)'; a spouse's pre-marriage loss is the spouse's carried loss. A help line could say so; low, no change needed.

i172 p. 3, 'Estates and trusts, include an NOL deduction on Form 1041.' A Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) of any kind is refused by scope.k1 (tick 'Income or a loss from a partnership, S corporation, estate or trust', 'A Yes ends the interview here').
i172 p. 3. The negative question 'not married to each other' is asked as a tick box ('You two were not married to each other when it arose'), which reads as a fact, not a double negative.

unruled:gate:s1.nol_separate#1.class: defect (low): the marital NOL questions name the loss year and later years, not a year the loss was carried back to
unruled:gate:s1.nol_separate#1.reason: Finding 0: a farming NOL carried back to an earlier joint year and then forward is not caught by 'the year any of the loss arose, or any year from then to 2024' (i172 p. 3, 'all years involved in figuring NOL carrybacks and carryovers'). Rare (farm losses are the only post-2017 carrybacks). Low. Finding 1 model error (the joint branch catches the remarried filer). Finding 2 is the scope.nol help low. Finding 3 presentation.

findings.evidence: i172 p. 3: 'filed a joint return for any or all of the tax years involved in figuring the NOL carryover' and 'all years involved in figuring NOL carrybacks and carryovers'. s1.nol_was_joint asks only the loss year and later; a joint carryback year is missed. Low.

i172 p. 3, Change in Marital Status. On mfj, s1.nol_joint asks s1.nol_not_married ('not married to each other in the year any of the loss arose, or in any year from then to 2025'); a filer remarried since the loss year answers Yes and is refused.
i172 p. 4, Excess Business Loss. Same scope.nol help low as gate:s1.nol_joint finding 1.
i172 p. 3. Signing a joint return, or amending to one, is filing a joint return; the tick 'A joint return was filed for a year it arose, or since' is passive and covers a return the spouse prepared.

unruled:gate:s1.uc_any#1.class: defect (low): the gate's help points to the form instead of the payment
unruled:gate:s1.uc_any#1.reason: The question 'In 2025, did you ... get unemployment benefits?' is right; the help 'The state sends Form 1099-G for them' is the only text, and findings 0 to 4 are filers who were paid benefits but may answer No: no form in the mail (posted online), benefits offset or intercepted, back benefits for 2024 paid in 2025, benefits repaid in 2025. Each is a plausible misreading; one help sentence answers all. Low.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 89, line 7 TIP: 'your state may issue an electronic Form 1099-G instead of it being mailed to you'. The help 'The state sends Form 1099-G for them' suggests a mailed form. Low.

i1040gi p. 89, line 7. Federal and railroad programs are still unemployment benefits, and the question asks about benefits, not the issuer; the help describes the usual case. Low, rides with the help fix.
i1040gi p. 89, 'the total unemployment compensation paid to you in 2025'. Benefits offset, intercepted or withheld were paid to the filer; 'get' with no help invites a No. Low.
i1040gi p. 89, 'paid to you in 2025'. Back benefits for 2024 weeks paid in 2025 are 2025 income; the help can say so. Low.
i1040gi p. 89, 'If you received an overpayment ... subtract the amount you repaid'. s1.uc_repaid handles a 2025 repayment once past the gate; the gate help can say to answer Yes even if repaid. Low.

unruled:gate:s1.winnings_any#1.class: defect: the gate asks what was won in 2025, not what was received
unruled:gate:s1.winnings_any#1.reason: Findings 0 to 2, 6: amounts received in 2025 on a prize won earlier (lottery installments, a sale of lottery payment rights, USOPC prize money for the 2024 Games, a 2024 contest prize delivered in 2025) are truthful Noes to 'In 2025, did you ... win'. Findings 3, 4, 5 and 7 are plausible misreadings the same rewording answers (gross winnings in a losing year, a recognition award, prize points, a sweepstakes). Medium.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 33, Installment payments: 'include in your gross income the annual payments and any amounts you receive designated as interest on the unpaid installments'. Truthful No to 'In 2025, did you ... win'. Medium.

i1040gi p. 91, Line 8b, 'a lump-sum payment from the sale of a right to receive future lottery payments'; p525 p. 33, 'report the amount you receive from the sale as ordinary income (on Schedule 1, line 8b) in the year you receive it'. Truthful No.

i1040gi p. 91, Line 8m. USOPC prize money for the 2024 Games received in 2025 is a truthful No to 'win in 2025'; the s1.olympic refusal is missed (amount effect only above the $1 million AGI limit). Low part of the same fix.

p525 p. 33, gambling winnings are included and losses deducted separately. The gate help says nothing about a losing year; s1.gambling_winnings ('before subtracting any losses') comes only after a Yes. Same fix.

p525 p. 35, Pulitzer, Nobel, and similar prizes: 'you must generally include the value of the prize in your income'. 'win money or a prize ... from ... an award' invites a No from an honoree who entered no contest. Same fix.
p525 p. 35, Prize points, 'taxable in the year they're paid or made available to you'. Named only in the gated s1.prizes help. Same fix.
p525 p. 35, Prizes and awards. A prize won in December 2024 and received in 2025; the gate is keyed to the win. Same fix.
p525 p. 35, 'a lucky number drawing, television or radio quiz program, beauty contest, or other event'. A sweepstakes or giveaway is a drawing; the list can name it. Low part of the same fix.

unruled:gate:s1.has_sc#1.class: low defect: the look-back question misses a contract adjusted in 2025 (BUG-0821); no gate defect otherwise
unruled:gate:s1.has_sc#1.reason: The gate is the count of Schedules C. Every no-Schedule-C case raised is refused before it matters: a K-1 by scope.k1, a farm or crop-share land by scope.farm, a vessel or equipment rented out by scope.rent_personal, an oil or gas working interest or the filer's own royalties by royalty.business, a rental's car or truck costs by rental.vehicle, and a rental treated as a QBI trade or business by sche.qbi_business. Schedule J is an election: a No yields a correct return without averaging. The one real miss is a long-term contract adjusted, not finished, in 2025 (i6251 p. 7).

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 110, Line 22 column (ii), quoted correctly. A rental's car interest is a Schedule E line 6 cost: rental.vehicle ('Car, truck or travel costs for it'; 'A Yes ends the interview here') refuses it. A farm is refused by scope.farm. So column (ii) can be non-zero only through a Schedule C, which is the gate.

As finding 0: a rental's vehicle costs are refused by rental.vehicle, so no part of the loan interest can be on Schedule E on a completed return; the 'own business' wording only has to reach Schedule C.

i8995 pp. 3-4, quoted correctly. Without a Schedule C the tool has no QBI business: K-1 refused (scope.k1), farm (scope.farm), rental as a trade or business (sche.qbi_business refuses; qbi.yaml note: QBI only of Schedule C businesses). A freed passive rental loss is figured by Form 8582 but carries no QBI. A closed sole proprietorship's allowed loss is deducted on a 2025 Schedule C, which sets the gate.

qbi.suspended asks 'deducting a business loss or expense of an earlier year that a tax limit kept you from deducting then'; a section 179 or 163(j) carryover is exactly that, and the help's 'Examples are' marks the list as examples. A rental is outside QBI here (sche.qbi_business refuses). Medium overstated; no change needed.

i6251 p. 7, Lines 2q and 2t, quoted correctly. A K-1's IDCs or mining costs are refused by scope.k1; a working interest held directly and reported on Schedule E is refused by royalty.business ('from an oil or gas working interest'); depletion by royalty.depletion and rental.depletion.
A drilling-partnership investor holds a Schedule K-1, refused by scope.k1 before s2.amt_business is reached.

f1040s2 line 17n, quoted correctly. A partner's or S corporation shareholder's look-back interest comes through a K-1 (scope.k1 refuses); an author's forecast-method book is refused via royalty.business. A passive film-rights investor on Schedule E is a residual too rare for its own entry (noted in BUG-0821).

i6251 p. 7, Line 2p: 'for the tax year the contract is completed or adjusted', checked. s2.lookback asks only whether the filer 'finish[ed] a contract in 2025'; an adjustment in 2025 to an earlier contract is a truthful No and line 17n is dropped. The income-forecast case is covered by the help ('Yes also for a film, book or similar property depreciated by its forecast income (Form 8866)'). Low.

i1040gi p. 36 and i1040sj p. 1, quoted correctly. A Schedule F farmer and a crop-share landlord are refused by scope.farm (help: 'Count a farm you run and a share of crops or livestock from land you let a farmer use'); a fishing-vessel lessor by scope.rent_personal. Schedule J is an election; a No gives a correct return without averaging.

i1040sj p. 1 crew-member clause, checked. A share-of-catch crew member has a Schedule C, so the gate holds. Schedule J is optional ('This is a choice ... to go on without it, answer No'), so a misread No yields a correct return without the election; no value is wrong. Wording could say 'your or your spouse's business'; low, not filed.

i1040gi p. 93, Line 16, quoted correctly. A partner's self-employment income comes through a K-1 (scope.k1 refuses) and a Schedule F farmer is refused by scope.farm, both before scope.se_plan_other is reached.

unruled:gate:s1.hobby_any#1.class: defect (medium): 'make money' reads as net profit, so a hobby run at a loss or paid in kind drops its receipts (BUG-0822)
unruled:gate:s1.hobby_any#1.reason: Line 8j takes gross receipts of an activity not engaged in for profit (p525 p. 31), and the amount help says costs are not subtracted, but the gate asks whether the filer 'made money'. A recreational farm is refused by scope.farm; an activity with business trappings reaches Schedule C, where sc.special screens a not-for-profit activity or hobby.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 31, 'You must include on your return income from an activity, even if you don't expect to make a profit from that activity', checked. The gate's 'make money from a hobby' is a truthful or plausible No for a hobby whose costs exceeded receipts, and s1.line8j is then zero. Medium (a misreading of everyday words rather than a truthful No).

Barter, goods or digital assets received are income under p525 p. 31 ('income from an activity'); 'make money' reads as cash. Same rewording; the fix adds goods and other payment and asks fair market value in the amount help.

p525 p. 31, 'a farm you operate mostly for recreation and pleasure', checked. A horse or cattle farm is refused by scope.farm ('income or a loss from farming'; help counts 'a farm you run'). Dog breeding run for pleasure is plainly a hobby or pastime; the residual is presentation.

A filer who considers the activity 'run as a business' reports its receipts on Schedule C, so nothing is dropped; sc.special lists 'an activity that is not a business (for example a sporadic activity, a not-for-profit activity or a hobby)' and refuses it.

unruled:gate:s1.inmate_wages#1.class: low defect: the gate's place wording ('in a jail or prison') misses work release and other correctional facilities (BUG-0823)
unruled:gate:s1.inmate_wages#1.reason: Line 8u is a status test, services performed while an inmate in a penal institution (i1040gi p. 92); the gate asks about work done 'while in a jail or prison'. The 2025 timing reads correctly ('In 2025, were you ... paid'), and home confinement is not a penal institution on the archived text.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8u, quoted correctly; p. 23, Line 1a: 'Do not report these wages on line 1a'. A work-release inmate working at an outside employer can truthfully read 'work done while in a jail or prison' as No: W-2 pay stays on line 1a and counts as EIC earned income (p596: earnings while an inmate 'aren't earned income'), 1099 pay is dropped. Rare; low (the reviewer's high assumes the place reading is the only one).
'Penal institution' (i1040gi p. 92) is wider than 'jail or prison'; a camp, detention or reentry center is a plausible No. Same rewording.

The gate reads 'In 2025, were you ... paid for work done while in a jail or prison?': 'In 2025' attaches to being paid, which is what line 8u counts ('the amount that you received'). A filer paid in 2025 for 2024 work answers Yes on the natural reading.

Pay credited to a trust or commissary account, or taken for restitution or fees, was received (i1040gi p. 92, 'the amount that you received'); a filer may not see it as 'paid'. The help sentence proposed in BUG-0823 covers it; low.

i1040gi p. 92 and p596 speak of an inmate 'in a penal institution'; nothing archived treats home confinement as being in a penal institution, and the reviewer says only that the filer 'may' be treated as an inmate. A No is the answer the archived text supports.

unruled:gate:s1.jury_any#1.class: low defect: 'paid for serving on a jury' can exclude jury-pool fees and pay signed over to an employer (BUG-0824)
unruled:gate:s1.jury_any#1.reason: Line 8h takes any jury duty pay (i1040gi p. 91; p525 p. 34). The gate's 'serving on a jury' can exclude jury-pool attendance fees, and it does not say that pay handed to an employer counts. Timing, per diem labels and grand juries are read correctly on the plain words.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 91, 'Enter any jury duty pay'; p525 p. 34, checked. A filer paid for days in the jury pool but not empanelled can truthfully say they did not serve on a jury; line 8h drops the fees. Small amounts; low (not high).

'In 2025, were you ... paid for serving on a jury?': 'In 2025' attaches to 'paid', and line 8h counts pay received (p525 p. 34, 'Jury duty pay you receive'). A December 2024 juror paid in January 2025 answers Yes on the natural reading.

p525 p. 34, quoted correctly. A No here zeroes both line 8h and line 24a (s1.has_jury_pay), so AGI is unchanged; the return omits a matched pair. The proposed gate wording of BUG-0824 adds 'pay you gave to your employer'.

A court's fee, per diem or attendance allowance for jury duty is what a filer reads as being 'paid' for it; no source text distinguishes them. The amount question asks 'How much jury pay'. No change beyond BUG-0824.
A grand jury is a jury; 'serving on a jury' includes it on its plain words, and p525 p. 34 makes no distinction. No change needed.

unruled:gate:s1.scholarship_any#1.class: low defect: 'a grant for study' and the Pell-grant help can lead a research fellow or a stipend recipient to answer No (BUG-0825)
unruled:gate:s1.scholarship_any#1.reason: Line 8r takes scholarship and fellowship grants not on a W-2 (i1040gi p. 92). The gate's 'for study' and its help, which names only Pell grants and payments to the school, can lead a research fellow or a stipend recipient to answer No. Athletic scholarships, service-conditioned grants and the timing are read correctly on the plain words.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8r, checked. A non-enrolled postdoctoral fellow paid a stipend with no W-2 may read 'a scholarship, a fellowship or a grant for study' as student aid; the whole fellowship then drops from line 8r. Plausible misreading, not a truthful No ('a fellowship' is named); low.

i1040gi p. 92, 'amounts used for room, board, and travel must be reported on line 8r', checked. A fellowship stipend paid to the student is a fellowship grant, but the help speaks only of Pell grants and grants paid to the school. The proposed help names stipends and living allowances. Low.

An athletic, housing or merit scholarship is 'a scholarship' on the plain words of the gate; 'for study' trails the third noun. The amount question asks for the room, board and travel part. No change beyond BUG-0825.

p525 p. 35, Payment for services, quoted correctly. A Fulbright grant is a grant; a teaching or research assistant's pay is normally on a W-2 (then left out, per the amount help). A tuition waiver is a scholarship. The amount question names 'pay for teaching, research or other work the grant required'. No change beyond BUG-0825.
'In 2025, did you ... get' reads as receipt in 2025, which is what line 8r takes. A filer whose 2024 award was paid in 2025 got it in 2025. No change needed.

unruled:gate:s1.stock_options_if_options.class: low defect: 'from an employer' excludes options inherited or received in a divorce (BUG-0826); the sale case is covered by the interview wording
unruled:gate:s1.stock_options_if_options.reason: The filer reads s2.options_any as 'In 2025, did you ... use stock options from an employer to buy shares, or sell shares bought that way?' with 'Count shares bought through an employee stock purchase plan', so a 2025 sale of ISO or ESPP shares bought earlier is a Yes (the reviewer saw the form label, which omits the sale). Options held by an heir or a former spouse are a truthful No.

findings.evidence: s2.options_any prompt: 'or sell shares bought that way?', help: 'Count shares bought through an employee stock purchase plan.' A disqualifying disposition in 2025 of 2024 ISO or ESPP shares is a Yes; s1.stock_options help names this case ('sold early and the employer did not add the income to a W-2').

i1040gi p. 91, Line 8k, 'any income from the exercise of stock options', checked. An heir exercising a deceased employee's nonstatutory options never had an employer that granted them; a truthful No drops the line 8k income. Rare; low (not high).
As finding 1, for options transferred in a divorce. Rare; low.

A director's or consultant's option income is nonemployee compensation, normally reported as Schedule C gross receipts (sc.yaml: 'including amounts properly shown on Forms 1099-NEC'), so it is not usually dropped; the proposed wording names the company the filer served. Low.
The prompt says 'stock options from an employer', not the current employer, and its help says 'Count shares bought through an employee stock purchase plan'. Both cases are a Yes.
A cashless exercise-and-sale both uses options to buy shares and sells shares bought that way; either half of the prompt gives Yes.

unruled:gate:sa.medical_asked#1.class: defect (low): estate payments for a decedent's final return are not reached by the gate; the other findings are covered or wording
unruled:gate:sa.medical_asked#1.reason: The review saw the helper labels (finding 0's 'money already taxed'); the interview asks sa.medical_premiums as 'pay for health insurance yourselves, not through a job: for example Medicare, a Marketplace plan, COBRA or long-term care insurance', with help naming Medicare taken from social security, and sa.medical_any's help counts insurance and says 'If you are not sure, answer Yes.' Finding 2, estate payments made in 2026 for a final return, is a low defect: the estate rule is only in sa.line1's help. The rest are wording residuals.

findings.evidence: i1040sca p. 1, Medicare Part B and D premiums. sa.medical_premiums (interview prompt above) asks about any self-paid insurance, Medicare named, with no 'already taxed' condition; a Yes asks sa.line1.

i1040sca p. 1, '7.5% of ... adjusted gross income ... line 11b'. sa.medical_any's help gives an example and says 'If you are not sure, answer Yes.' The filer cannot know AGI in advance; wording residual, low.

i1040sca p. 1, 'Certain medical expenses paid out of a deceased taxpayer's estate can be claimed on the deceased taxpayer's final return'; p502, Whose Medical Expenses Can You Include, Decedent, 'expenses paid by the decedent's estate ... as paid by the decedent at the time the medical services were provided ... paid within the 1-year period beginning with the day after the date of death.' The gate asks costs 'paid in 2025' by the filer or spouse; the estate rule is only in sa.line1's help, behind the gate.

p502, What Expenses Can You Include This Year?, 'include medical expenses you charge to your credit card in the year the charge is made'; i1040sca p. 2, bills paid in 2025. The gate asks costs paid in 2025; a payment in 2025 for 2024 care is a 2025 payment by its words. Low wording.

i1040sca p. 2, 'If you received a reimbursement in 2025 for prior year medical or dental expenses, don't reduce your 2025 expenses'. sa.line1 says so; the gate's 'less anything insurance paid back' could be over-applied. Low.

i1040sca pp. 1-2 (nursing help, travel, lodging); p502 special schooling. sa.medical_any's help lists doctors, dentists, hospitals, prescriptions and insurance as examples and says 'If you are not sure, answer Yes'; a threshold gate cannot list Publication 502. Low.
p502 p. 12, repaid advance PTC. A Marketplace enrollee is asked sa.medical_premiums ('a Marketplace plan'), and sa.line1 states the Form 8962 rule.
Both sa.medical_any and sa.medical_premiums say '(or, on a joint return, your spouse)'; the review read the helper label.

unruled:gate:sa.mfs_spouse_not_itemizing.class: defect (low): sa.spouse_extra's wording (no definition of blind, a three-way conjunction, a spouse who died after 65)
unruled:gate:sa.mfs_spouse_not_itemizing.reason: The gate is computed (MFS and the spouse not itemizing); the findings are about the gated question sa.spouse_extra, whose Yes refuses. A wrong No omits the spouse's boxes on line 12d. Finding 0 repeats the instructions' own words ('had no income'); the gross-income reading rests on section 151(b), not on the archived text. Findings 1 to 3 are one low wording defect.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d, 'if your spouse had no income, isn't filing a return'. sa.spouse_extra asks 'Did your husband or wife have no income in 2025', the instructions' words; the archived pages do not define income here.

i1040gi p. 33, Blindness, 'You can't see better than 20/200 in your better eye ... or Your field of vision is 20 degrees or less.' person.blind gives this definition for the filer; sa.spouse_extra says only 'blind at the end of 2025'.

sa.spouse_extra: 'Did your husband or wife have no income in 2025, and are they filing no 2025 return, and were they born before January 2, 1961, or blind at the end of 2025?' with help 'A Yes ends the interview here.' The double negative 'are they filing no 2025 return' in a three-part conjunction invites a No from a filer whose spouse is not filing.

i1040gi p. 33, Death of spouse in 2025, 'Your spouse is considered age 65 at the time of death. Check the appropriate box for your spouse.' The present-tense wording does not say a spouse who died in 2025 counts. Low.

unruled:gate:sa.personal_property_tax_an.class: defect (low): the gate help excludes a partly weight-based fee; the rest covered or wording
unruled:gate:sa.personal_property_tax_an.reason: Finding 1 is the same low defect as the screen review's finding 0. Finding 0 is covered through sa.state_tax_other (line 5a). Findings 2 to 5 are wording residuals; the help already says some states charge it with the yearly registration.

findings.evidence: i1040sca p. 3, Safe harbor. sa.state_tax_other includes 'the part of the credit you used against state or local tax', which enters line 5a; lines 5d and 5e are the same as with 5c. Its gate sa.state_tax_other_any's help names 'a state tax credit for a gift to charity that you applied to your tax'.

i1040sca p. 6, Line 5c, 'Part of the fee was based on the car's value and part was based on its weight. You can deduct only the part of the fee that was based on the car's value.' The gate help: 'A flat fee, or one based on weight, does not count.'
i1040sca p. 6, Line 5c example (registration fee). The gate help: 'Some states and towns charge it with the yearly registration of a car.' Low; names of state charges are wording.
i1040sca p. 6, 'based on value alone and ... imposed on a yearly basis'. A filer who cannot tell whether the bill is value-based must check it; the gate asks the IRS's own test. Low.
i1040sca p. 7, 'Only taxes paid in 2025 and assessed prior to 2026'. A prorated first-year bill or a late-paid earlier bill is still a yearly tax paid in 2025. Low.
i1040sca p. 6, Line 5c. 'a car, a boat or other belongings' covers an aircraft, trailer or mobile home taxed as personal property. Low.

unruled:gate:sa.state_tax_any#1.class: no gate defect; tax withheld from other income and state fund contributions are asked by sa.state_tax_other_any
unruled:gate:sa.state_tax_any#1.reason: sa.line5a_if_state_tax is W-2 withholding only (boxes 17 and 19). Withholding from a pension, unemployment, winnings or other payments and mandatory state fund contributions belong to the sibling sa.state_tax_other_any (asked of every filer in the same tick-box screen, 'Paid other state or local income tax, or a state disability fund'), whose amount sa.state_tax_other is added in sa.line5a_total. Its own wording gaps are ruled under gate:sa.state_tax_other_any.

findings.evidence: i1040sca p. 3, Line 5a, 'Forms W-2G, 1099-G, 1099-R, 1099-MISC, and 1099-NEC may also show state and local income taxes withheld'. sa.state_tax_other_any's help: 'Count state tax taken out of a pension, unemployment pay or winnings'; sa.state_tax_other adds 'tax taken out of other income'; sa.line5a_total sums both. The 1099-NEC/MISC wording gap is the defect ruled under sa.state_tax_other_any (BUG-0815).

i1040sca p. 3, Line 5a, mandatory disability, unemployment and family leave fund contributions. sa.state_tax_other_any: 'or pay into a state disability or family leave fund?', help '(box 14 or 19 of a W-2: SDI, SUI, FLI)'; sa.state_tax_other lists the funds.
i1040sca p. 3, Line 5a. A city wage tax or earned income tax is a local income tax taken out of pay; it is normally in box 19. A box-14-only local tax is rare; low wording.

unruled:gate:sa.state_tax_other_any#1.class: defect (medium): a prior-year refund applied to 2025 estimates and non-pension withholding are not named by the gate
unruled:gate:sa.state_tax_other_any#1.reason: Finding 0 (a credited 2024 overpayment) is the main defect, and finding 3 (1099-R IRA, 1099-NEC/MISC withholding) joins it: both amounts are in the gated sa.state_tax_other's list but not in the gate's question or help. Findings 1, 2 and 4 to 6 are wording residuals that the same fix can absorb.

findings.evidence: i1040sca p. 3, Line 5a, 'State and local estimated tax payments made during 2025, including any part of a prior year refund that you chose to have credited to your 2025 state or local income taxes.' The gate asks whether the filer paid 'in another way, such as estimated payments or a payment with a state return'; the help does not name a credited refund. sa.state_tax_other does, but only behind the gate.
i1040sca p. 3, Line 5a, taxes paid in 2025 for a prior year. A January 2025 estimated payment is an 'estimated payment' made in 2025, and the gate names 'a payment with a state return'. Low.
i1040sca p. 3, Line 5a. An extension or assessment payment is a payment of state income tax 'in another way'; the gate's items are examples. Low; the P2 fix can name them.
i1040sca p. 3, Line 5a, 'Forms W-2G, 1099-G, 1099-R, 1099-MISC, and 1099-NEC may also show state and local income taxes withheld'. The help names only 'a pension, unemployment pay or winnings'.

i1040sca p. 3, Line 5a. Nonresident or composite tax paid for a partner, or withholding on a real property sale, is not on the archived pages by name; the gate's 'pay state or local income tax in another way' reaches it by its words. Low; the P2 fix can add K-1 withholding.

i1040sca p. 3, Safe harbor, 'treat this amount as state or local tax paid in the year the credit is applied'. The help's 'a state tax credit for a gift to charity that you applied to your tax' follows the instructions; timing is the safe harbor's rule. Low.
i1040sca p. 3, U.S. territory taxes. The gate's help names 'income tax of a U.S. territory'. Low.

unruled:gate:sa.has_mortgage_interest#1.class: defect: the other-use question drops 'substantially'; the line 8a gate itself is sound
unruled:gate:sa.has_mortgage_interest#1.reason: Findings 0 and 1 (interest or points only on line 8b or 8c) are covered: lines 8b and 8c are zero here and any interest or points not on the filer's own Form 1098 are refused by sa.mortgage_unreported, asked of every filer with a home, so the line 8a gate drops nothing. Finding 2 is the wording defect BUG-0805. Findings 3 and 4 are presentation or covered by the help.

findings.evidence: i1040sca p. 8, Line 8b, 'If you paid home mortgage interest to a recipient who didn't provide you a Form 1098, report your deductible mortgage interest on line 8b'; More than one borrower, 'If the shared interest was reported on the other person's Form 1098, report your share of the interest on line 8b'. Lines 8b and 8c are fixed at zero in this tool: sa.mortgage_unreported ('Did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) pay mortgage interest or points in 2025 that no Form 1098 in your name shows, for example to a person who sold you the home, or on a loan whose Form 1098 went to a co-borrower?') is asked of every filer with sa.home_asked, independent of line 8a, and a Yes refuses through sa.unsupported (checked: an eval of a fixture case with sa.mortgage_unreported true gives the 'Schedule A unsupported item' refusal). A return whose interest is on line 8b or 8c is refused before any debt or use limit could matter, so gating the limit questions on line 8a loses nothing.

f1040sa line 8c, 'Points not reported to you on Form 1098'. sa.mortgage_unreported asks for 'mortgage interest or points in 2025 that no Form 1098 in your name shows' and refuses on Yes (sa.unsupported); line 8c is fixed at zero.

i1040sca p. 8, Line 8, 'you didn't use all of your home mortgage proceeds from those loans to buy, build, or substantially improve your home'; Limits, 'to the extent that the loan proceeds ... are used to buy, build, or substantially improve the home securing the loan'. The line sa.mortgage_other_use says 'substantially improve', but the interview prompt asks 'Was any of the money borrowed against your home used for something other than buying, building or improving it', and the help says 'A loan used only to buy or build the home ... is a No'. A filer who spent home-equity money on repairs or furnishings can truthfully answer No, the refusal is missed and the limited interest is deducted in full.

i1040sca p. 8, 'A home mortgage is any loan that is secured by your main home or second home'. The question follows sa.mortgage_interest, which asks the interest of 'you (or, on a joint return, your spouse)', and asks about 'money borrowed against your home'; on a joint return 'your home' reads as the couple's home. A spouse's separate loan on the couple's home is unlikely to be left out. Wording could name the spouse; low, no defect filed.

i1040sca p. 8, 'you had one or more home mortgages in 2025 with an outstanding balance and you didn't use all of your home mortgage proceeds'. The question is not limited to 2025 borrowing ('Was any of the money borrowed against your home used ...'), and the help says only 'a refinancing for no more than was still owed on such a loan, is a No', so a cash-out refinance, old or new, is a Yes by its terms. Rolled-in closing costs are a Pub. 936 detail, not in the archived instructions.

unruled:gate:sa.mortgage_interest_mfs#1.class: no gate defect; line 8b interest is refused by sa.mortgage_unreported
unruled:gate:sa.mortgage_interest_mfs#1.reason: Finding 0 covered by the sa.mortgage_unreported refusal. Findings 1 to 3 are wording of sa.mortgage_over_limit_mfs (boat or co-op as a home, HELOC, per-home value), presentation: the question asks about 'the loans on your home', which takes in a HELOC however labeled, and its help counts a second home; no defect filed.

findings.evidence: i1040sca p. 8, Line 8b, 'If you paid home mortgage interest to a recipient who didn't provide you a Form 1098, report your deductible mortgage interest on line 8b'; More than one borrower, 'If the shared interest was reported on the other person's Form 1098, report your share of the interest on line 8b'. Lines 8b and 8c are fixed at zero in this tool: sa.mortgage_unreported ('Did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) pay mortgage interest or points in 2025 that no Form 1098 in your name shows, for example to a person who sold you the home, or on a loan whose Form 1098 went to a co-borrower?') is asked of every filer with sa.home_asked, independent of line 8a, and a Yes refuses through sa.unsupported (checked: an eval of a fixture case with sa.mortgage_unreported true gives the 'Schedule A unsupported item' refusal). A return whose interest is on line 8b or 8c is refused before any debt or use limit could matter, so gating the limit questions on line 8a loses nothing.

i1040sca p. 8, 'A home can be a house, condominium, cooperative, mobile home, boat, or similar property'. sa.home_other already defines a boat, camper or mobile home with sleeping, cooking and toilet facilities as a home, and the over-limit help says 'Count the loans on a second home too'. The over-limit help could repeat that a boat or RV can be the second home; low.

i1040sca p. 8, 'A home mortgage is any loan that is secured by your main home or second home, regardless of how the loan is labeled'. The prompt asks whether 'the loans on your home' add up to more than $375,000, not 'the mortgage', so a HELOC or a loan labeled personal but secured by the home is within its words. Low.
i1040sca p. 8, 'If the total amount of all mortgages is more than the fair market value of the home, see Pub. 936'. The prompt's 'more than the home is worth' follows the source's singular. Low.

unruled:gate:sa.mortgage_interest_not_mf.class: no gate defect; separate returns are asked by the MFS sibling, line 8b interest refused by sa.mortgage_unreported
unruled:gate:sa.mortgage_interest_not_mf.reason: Finding 0 is a model error: a separate return is asked sa.mortgage_over_limit_mfs through the sibling gate sa.mortgage_interest_mfs, with the $375,000/$500,000 limits. Finding 1 covered by the sa.mortgage_unreported refusal. Findings 2 to 5 are wording of sa.mortgage_over_limit, presentation or covered.

findings.evidence: i1040sca p. 8, '$750,000 ($375,000 if you are married filing separately)'. sa.mortgage_interest_mfs (line 8a above zero and sa.mfs) gates sa.mortgage_over_limit_mfs, 'Did the loans on your home add up to more than $375,000 at any time in 2025, or to more than the home is worth?', which refuses on Yes (sa.mortgage_over_limit_if_interest in sa.unsupported). The not-MFS gate is false for a separate return by design.

i1040sca p. 8, Line 8b, 'If you paid home mortgage interest to a recipient who didn't provide you a Form 1098, report your deductible mortgage interest on line 8b'; More than one borrower, 'If the shared interest was reported on the other person's Form 1098, report your share of the interest on line 8b'. Lines 8b and 8c are fixed at zero in this tool: sa.mortgage_unreported ('Did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) pay mortgage interest or points in 2025 that no Form 1098 in your name shows, for example to a person who sold you the home, or on a loan whose Form 1098 went to a co-borrower?') is asked of every filer with sa.home_asked, independent of line 8a, and a Yes refuses through sa.unsupported (checked: an eval of a fixture case with sa.mortgage_unreported true gives the 'Schedule A unsupported item' refusal). A return whose interest is on line 8b or 8c is refused before any debt or use limit could matter, so gating the limit questions on line 8a loses nothing.

i1040sca p. 8, 'A home mortgage is any loan that is secured by your main home or second home'. The prompt asks about 'the loans on your home' and the help says 'Count the loans on a second home too'; a spouse's second-home loan on a joint return is within those words, though not named (the MFS twin's help names the spouse's share). Low; no defect filed.

i1040sca p. 8, 'A home can be a house, condominium, cooperative, mobile home, boat, or similar property'. As the MFS twin: sa.home_other defines a boat, camper or mobile home as a home; the over-limit help counts a second home. Low.

i1040sca p. 8, 'If the total amount of all mortgages is more than the fair market value of the home, see Pub. 936'. The prompt follows the source's singular 'the home'; market value versus assessed value is a Pub. 936 detail. Low.

i1040sca p. 8, limits for debt before and after December 15, 2017. The help says 'If all of it was borrowed on or before December 15, 2017, the limit is $1,000,000'; an amount added in a later refinance was borrowed after that date, so the $750,000 test applies by the help's own words.

unruled:gate:sa.property_tax_other_if_ho.class: no gate defect; business, unowned and escrow cases are excluded by the line 5b amount question
unruled:gate:sa.property_tax_other_if_ho.reason: Findings 0 to 3 covered by the sa.line5b question and help and the leave-out list. Finding 4 is a model error: sa.home_owner asks about 'you (or, on a joint return, your spouse)'. Findings 5 and 6 are presentation residuals (the help equates billing with assessment; the buyer's payment of the seller's share at closing is a Pub. 530 rule not in the archived instructions); no defect filed.

findings.evidence: i1040sca p. 6, Line 5b, 'real estate you own that wasn't used for business'. sa.line5b asks 'How much property tax did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) pay in 2025 on your home and on any other real estate you own that is not used for business?'; tax on a rental or business part is not asked into the amount.

i1040sca p. 6, 'assessed uniformly at a like rate on all real property throughout the community, and the proceeds are used for general community or governmental purposes'. The leave-out list names 'a special tax charged only on some properties' and 'a charge for a service, such as trash collection or water'.

i1040sca p. 6, 'taxes you paid on real estate you own'. sa.line5b asks 'How much property tax did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) pay in 2025 on your home and on any other real estate you own that is not used for business?'; tax on another person's property is outside the amount asked.

i1040sca p. 6, 'you can include only the amount the mortgage company actually paid to the taxing authority in 2025'. sa.line5b help: 'If your lender pays the tax for you, box 10 of Form 1098 or the lender's year-end statement shows what it paid in 2025.'
sa.home_owner asks 'At any time in 2025, did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) own a home or other real estate?'; the reviewer saw only the gate's label. The spouse's real estate is counted.

i1040sca p. 6, 'State or local law determines whether and when a property tax is assessed, which is generally when the taxpayer becomes liable for the property tax imposed'. The list item '2026 tax paid before it was billed' with the help 'Tax is billed when it is assessed under state or local law' carries the rule through billing; an early bill issued before legal assessment is rare. Low; the help could say 'when state or local law makes you liable for it'.

i1040sca p. 6 says only 'Any real estate taxes you paid at closing should be shown on your settlement statement'; the rule that a buyer's payment of the seller's share is not the buyer's deduction is in Pub. 530, not archived. The amount question asks tax on 'real estate you own'. Low; no defect filed.

unruled:gate:sa.home_asked#1.class: no gate defect in the condition; low wording residual for a land-contract buyer (BUG-0807)
unruled:gate:sa.home_asked#1.reason: Finding 0 is a model error: the second helper's question sa.home_other asks about 'you (or, on a joint return, your spouse)'; the reviewer saw only its label. Finding 1 covered (the sa.home_owner help names a co-op apartment). Finding 2 is an open residual, low: a buyer on a land contract may answer No to owning, and is then asked neither line 5b nor the unreported-interest refusal (BUG-0807). Finding 3 presentation (the help counts land; a deeded timeshare is rare).

findings.evidence: sa.home_other asks 'In 2025, did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) pay interest on a loan for a boat, camper or mobile home you can live in, or on a mortgage for a home that is in someone else's name?'; the prompt the reviewer saw showed the helper's label, which omits the spouse.
i1040sca p. 8, 'A home can be a house, condominium, cooperative'. sa.home_owner help: 'Count a house, a condo or co-op apartment, a mobile home, a vacation home and land'.

i1040sca p. 9, Line 8b, 'If you paid home mortgage interest to the person from whom you bought the home and that person didn't provide you a Form 1098'; p. 6, Line 5b, 'real estate you own'. Neither sa.home_owner nor its help says that a home being bought on a land contract or contract for deed counts, and sa.home_other speaks of 'a mortgage for a home that is in someone else's name'. A buyer who answers No to both gets no line 5b or 8 amount and is never asked sa.mortgage_unreported, so the refusal for seller-financed interest is missed and the property tax deduction is dropped. Understated deduction, rare; low.

i1040sca p. 6, 'real estate you own'. The sa.home_owner prompt says 'a home or other real estate' and its help counts 'land'; a share of land owned with relatives is real estate owned. A deeded timeshare is rare and not named. Low.

unruled:gate:oi8z.damages#1.class: defect (low): medical care for non-physical emotional distress and pre-September-1995 agreements (BUG-0804); the kind gate itself is sound
unruled:gate:oi8z.damages#1.reason: Findings 3 and 4 are BUG-0804 (overlaps completeness oi8z#1.1). Finding 0 presentation (the kind label names punitive damages as its example). Finding 1 presentation (a negotiated claim is a 'case' in ordinary use; the line says 'damages or this settlement'). Findings 2 and 5 covered: the question asks whether the case was about a physical injury, of anyone.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 32, 'Punitive damages in most cases. It doesn't matter if they relate to a physical injury'. The kind label 'Taxable damages or a settlement, such as punitive damages' names punitive damages as the example, so a filer with punitive damages is pointed to this kind. A filer who leaves the whole award off the return is not reachable by any gate. Low.

p525 p. 32, 'settlement amounts you receive by compromise or judgment'. The kind label says 'damages or a settlement' and oi8z.injury asks 'paid in a case about a physical injury'; an insurance claim settled without a suit is commonly called a case. Wording could say 'a claim or lawsuit'; low.

p525 p. 32, emotional distress due to a physical injury. The question asks whether the case was 'about a physical injury', which a physical assault or accident case is, whatever the damages were labeled; Yes refuses.

p525 p. 32, Emotional distress, 'you must include the damages in your income, except for any damages you receive for medical care due to that emotional distress'; Pre-existing agreement, 'If you receive damages under a written binding agreement, court decree, or mediation award that was in effect (or issued on or before) September 13, 1995, don't include in income any of those damages received on account of personal injuries or sickness'. oi8z.injury asks only 'Was any of it paid in a case about a physical injury or a physical sickness?' (refusal oi8z.injury_if_damages on Yes); neither the medical-care part of non-physical emotional-distress damages nor pre-1995 agreements are asked or refused, and oi8z.amount ('How much of it is income for 2025?') gives no rule, so the whole award is included. Overstated income, rare. Overlaps completeness oi8z#1.1.

p525 p. 32, Emotional distress, 'you must include the damages in your income, except for any damages you receive for medical care due to that emotional distress'; Pre-existing agreement, 'If you receive damages under a written binding agreement, court decree, or mediation award that was in effect (or issued on or before) September 13, 1995, don't include in income any of those damages received on account of personal injuries or sickness'. oi8z.injury asks only 'Was any of it paid in a case about a physical injury or a physical sickness?' (refusal oi8z.injury_if_damages on Yes); neither the medical-care part of non-physical emotional-distress damages nor pre-1995 agreements are asked or refused, and oi8z.amount ('How much of it is income for 2025?') gives no rule, so the whole award is included. Overstated income, rare. Overlaps completeness oi8z#1.1.

p525 p. 32, 'compensatory damages for personal physical injury or physical sickness'. The prompt 'a case about a physical injury or a physical sickness' does not say whose; a wrongful-death or consortium case about a relative's injury is within it.

unruled:gate:tipjob.listed#1.class: defect (medium): the listed-occupation question reads as 'all of the work' (BUG-0806); other findings presentation
unruled:gate:tipjob.listed#1.reason: Finding 0 is BUG-0806. Findings 1 to 3 are presentation: the prompt's examples are examples ('are on it'), and the help links the whole list. Finding 4 covered: tipjob is asked under the person frame 'For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return)'.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 103, 'If you received tips as an employee in more than one occupation for the same employer, only those tips that were received in an occupation on the list ... are considered qualified tips'. tipjob.listed asks 'Is the work you got these tips for on the IRS list of jobs that customarily get tips?', and its help says 'If the work is not on it, tips from this employer cannot be deducted and nothing more is asked about them'. A filer with tips from one employer for a listed and an unlisted job can read the work as a whole as not listed and answer No: tipjob.amount is then zero, the listed tips' deduction is dropped, and the refusal for mixed tips (tipjob.other_work, which exists for this case) is never reached.

i1040gi p. 103, the occupation list. The prompt gives examples ('Restaurant, bar and hotel staff, hairdressers and barbers, and taxi and delivery drivers are on it') and the help says 'The whole list is at IRS.gov/TippedOccupations'. Could add 'for example' and the category headings; low.
i1040gi pp. 102-103, the list gives occupation descriptions and illustrative examples. The help points to the whole list; matching duties rather than titles could be said. Low.

i1040gi p. 102, 'working in an occupation that customarily and regularly received tips'. The prompt asks about 'the work you got these tips for', an occupation, though its examples name places ('Restaurant, bar and hotel staff'). Low.

i1040gi p. 101, 'You (and/or your spouse if filing a joint return)'. The tipjob roster is asked under the person frame 'For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return) —', so the questions are about the person whose employer it is.

unruled:gate:div.capital_gain_boxes#1.class: defect (medium): the box question excludes amounts without a form and shares of forms in another name
unruled:gate:div.capital_gain_boxes#1.reason: Findings 0 and 1 are BUG-0830; the corrected-form case is not a defect; 2f is refused.

unruled:gate:f1116col.has_div#1.class: no gate defect: no amount turns on the dividend/interest split; K-1 refused
unruled:gate:f1116col.has_div#1.reason: Dividends and interest of a column go to the same line 1a and line 8; a misclassification is caught by f1116.income_over or changes nothing.

unruled:gate:f8853c.has_line17#1.class: no gate defect; the box 4 and box 3 readings follow the payee statement the line instructions name; low wording points

findings.evidence: i8853 p. 8, Qualified LTC Insurance Contract, 'Before January 1, 1997, that met state law requirements ... and hasn't been changed materially'. f8853 line 17, 'Enter the total of the amounts from box 1 of all Forms 1099-LTC you received with respect to the insured on which the "Per diem" box in box 3 is checked'. Line 17 follows the form's box 3 by its own instruction, and f8853c.periodic asks the box 3 fact; a payment with no Form 1099-LTC is outside what line 17 describes.
f8853c.line17 is encoded for forms 'you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) received for this person', and Section C is one entry per insured person; the box 4 question is asked within that entry.

A filer who counts a life insurance form with box 4 blank answers Yes and is refused at f8853c.line26 (nonqualified_if_periodic). That is a wrong refusal, not a wrong No; line 17 is LTC per diem forms, and accelerated death benefits are line 19.
The help 'Box 4 of Form 1099-LTC is checked "Qualified contract" for most policies' states a fact and asks the filer to look at the box; low.

unruled:gate:f8853c.has_line24#1.class: defect (medium, wording): the pre-1996 question is in the past tense against an expected reimbursement; the general-rule reading is a model error
unruled:gate:f8853c.has_line24#1.reason: (0) model error: the filer is never shown the 'generally don't include' caution; the line 24 question asks every reimbursement, so pre-1996 amounts are entered and the pre-1996 question then refuses. findings.evidence: i8853 p. 9, Line 24 Caution, 'Generally, don't include on line 24 reimbursements ... under a contract issued before August 1, 1996'. i8853 p. 9, Line 24, 'Enter the reimbursements you received or expect to receive'. The gated question 'Was any of that paid back under a policy issued before August 1, 1996?' is past tense, while the encoding says 'received'; an expected pre-1996 reimbursement can be answered No and the refusal missed.

i8853 p. 9, 'you must include reimbursements if the contract was exchanged or modified after July 31, 1996, to increase per diem payments or reimbursements'. A filer who reads the replacement policy's date answers No and keeps the reimbursement on line 24; that lowers line 25 and raises line 26 (the tax is not understated). Low; the wording 'first issued' is in the fix.
The help is only 'A Yes ends the interview here.'; low, the question itself states the date test.

unruled:gate:f8853c.has_periodic#1.class: defect (medium, wording): line 24 asks only what was 'paid back to you'; others-paid omits a lump-sum accelerated death benefit to another person
unruled:gate:f8853c.has_periodic#1.reason: (0) defect: the others-paid question asks only about payments at a set rate, while line 15 names any accelerated death benefit to another person (BUG-0873). (1) presentation: with only terminally ill benefits line 26 is zero (Multiple Payees, 'skip lines 17 through 25 and enter -0- on line 26'), so line 15 changes no amount. (2, 3, 4) defect, medium: 'paid back to you' leaves out reimbursements paid to the provider, by Medicaid or the VA, or due in 2026, against line 24's 'received or expect to receive through insurance or otherwise' (BUG-0873). (5) covered: the rate question names 'a policy start or stop paying partway through', any policy for this person.

findings.evidence: f8853 line 15, 'did anyone other than you receive payments on a per diem or other periodic basis under a qualified LTC insurance contract covering the insured or receive accelerated death benefits under a life insurance policy covering the insured?'. The interview asks 'was anyone besides you ... also paid at a set rate under a policy on this person?', so an accelerated death benefit paid in one sum to a sibling is answered No and the Multiple Payees refusal (f8853c.line26) is not reached. Medium.

i8853 p. 9, Multiple Payees, 'If you checked "Yes" on lines 15 and 16 and the only payments you received were accelerated death benefits that were paid because the insured was terminally ill, skip lines 17 through 25 and enter -0- on line 26'. With line 20 zero, line 26 is zero whatever line 15 says; the gate changes no amount.

i8853 p. 9, Line 24, 'Enter the reimbursements you received or expect to receive through insurance or otherwise'. The interview asks 'How much of those care costs was paid back to you, by insurance or otherwise?'; benefits assigned and paid to the nursing home are not 'paid back to you', line 24 is understated and line 26 understated.
Same line 24 text, 'or expect to receive'; the past tense 'was paid back' leaves out a 2026 payment for December 2025 care, though the encoding (f8853c.line24) says 'received or expect to receive'.

Same text, 'through insurance or otherwise'. The help 'Count insurance or other payments that repaid those costs' reads past Medicaid or VA payments made to the facility, while line 22's help counts costs 'whoever paid them'.

i8853 p. 9, Method 2. The interview asks 'did the rate of those payments change, or did a policy start or stop paying partway through?', any policy paying for this person, LTC or life; the entry covers payments to either spouse. A Yes refuses.

unruled:gate:f8853c.periodic#1.class: no gate defect for the set-rate test; one wording residual: 'per day or month' omits a weekly or other period
unruled:gate:f8853c.periodic#1.reason: (0) defect, low to medium: the question names 'a set amount per day or month' though the encoding says 'per day, week or month' and the definition is any fixed periodic amount (BUG-0873); the box 3 'Per diem' mark the question names limits it. (4) model error: line 19 is 'Accelerated death benefits received on a per diem or other periodic basis'; a lump sum is not on it.

findings.evidence: i8853 p. 8, 'Per diem payments are payments of a fixed amount made on a periodic basis without regard to actual expenses incurred'. The interview asks 'Were any of the payments at a set amount per day or month, whatever the care cost ("Per diem" checked in box 3 ...)?'; the encoding (f8853c.periodic) says 'per day, week or month'. A weekly or quarterly fixed benefit may be answered No; the box 3 mark limits it.

The question says 'at a set amount ... whatever the care cost', which is the indemnity policy's fixed daily benefit; the help's 'Payments that only repaid care costs' describes reimbursement, the other box 3 mark.
f8853 line 17, 'all Forms 1099-LTC ... on which the "Per diem" box in box 3 is checked'; the line follows box 3 by its own instruction.

The question asks about 'any of the payments' for this person, which include accelerated death benefits (the entry's note: 'payments ... under a long-term care insurance contract, or accelerated death benefits under a life insurance contract'); periodic benefits from a life policy answer Yes and line 19 is then asked ('generally box 2 of Form 1099-LTC').

f8853 line 19, 'Accelerated death benefits received on a per diem or other periodic basis'; i8853 p. 8, accelerated death benefits and viatical settlements are 'fully excludable' when the insured is terminally ill and excludable 'to the same extent as ... a qualified LTC insurance contract' when chronically ill, the per diem limit reaching periodic payments. A lump sum is not a line 19 amount; the Filing Requirements chart asks about benefits 'made on a per diem or other periodic basis'.

The question asks whether any of the payments in 2025 were at a set rate; line 19's help, 'Leave out anything paid after a doctor certified that the person was expected to die within 24 months', follows i8853 p. 8, 'only include on line 19 payments received before the insured was certified as terminally ill'.

The help says 'A plan covering more than one person includes one for an employee and a child, and counts even if it did not cover you'; the question asks whether the other person 'had' such a plan, which includes coverage as a member.
A filer who does not know whether the former spouse's plan was an HDHP; low, the question gives the plain description and the other questions use the same term.

f8889.married_family is 'treated as having family coverage at any time during 2025', and f8889.spouse_family asks a married person with self-only coverage 'In any month of 2025, did your spouse have a high-deductible plan covering more than one person?' (help: 'both of you are treated as having family coverage').
The common prefix 'For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return)' on a separate return; the question names 'your husband or wife'. Low.

unruled:gate:f8889.testing_failed_figure.class: no gate defect; a 2025 funding distribution is refused, and a wrong No to the disability question refuses
unruled:gate:f8889.testing_failed_figure.reason: (0) covered: a 2025 funding distribution refuses at f8889.ira_transfer. i8889 p. 2, 'other than because of death or becoming disabled'. A No to f8889.disabled makes f8889.testing_failed true, which refuses (Part III); the wrong answer refuses rather than prepares a wrong return. The help's example is 'Medicare at 65'.
Same: a No refuses at f8889.testing_failed; the wording only sends a disabled filer to the refusal.

unruled:gate:ira.has_deduction#1.class: no gate defect; the help states what a No does; one presentation low on 'Almost everyone answers No'
unruled:gate:ira.has_deduction#1.reason: (0) covered: a No takes the full deduction the rules allow, which is a lawful return, and the help says so ('To go on with the full deduction, answer No'). findings.evidence: p590a p. 16, 'you can even designate otherwise deductible contributions as nondeductible contributions' (a choice). The help says 'To go on with the full deduction, answer No'; a filer who answers No gets the deduction the rules allow, a correct return for that choice.
The help 'Almost everyone answers No' leans the answer; the consequence of each answer is stated. Low.
The prompt is 'Do you want to deduct less of your (or, on a joint return, your spouse's) traditional IRA contributions ...'.

unruled:gate:ira.mfs_cov_matters#1.class: defect (low, wording): 'covered by a retirement plan at work' may leave out a self-employed spouse's plan
unruled:gate:ira.mfs_cov_matters#1.reason: (0) defect, low: BUG-0881. (1) covered: the help gives box 13 as a sign ('should be ticked'), the question asks the fact. (2) presentation: the help's list says what 'counts', not all that counts.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 96, covered 'at work or through self-employment'. The help 'A pension, a 401(k) or 403(b), or a SEP or SIMPLE IRA counts, even if they put nothing in' gives examples; a TSP or governmental pension is a pension or 401(k)-type plan. Low.

'The person who earned this pension or plan balance' is the participant, whoever passed it on.
